sentences.9: Former Lord Justice of Appeal, Sir Patrick Elias, said: 'The paper raises very serious concerns about the impartiality and independence of the CPS when dealing with the highly sensitive issue of the treatment of transgender persons. It appears to have adopted uncritically the controversial views of Stonewall.'
sentences.10: The report was released just as a new Director of Public Prosecutions - Stephen Parkinson - took up his post and last night, the CPS made clear that parts of the domestic abuse advice were now being reviewed.

Explanation.explanation: The argument refers to replacing current guidelines with something that follows British law instead of 'Stonewall law', appealing to the idea that traditional British law should take precedence over newer guidelines influenced by a particular organization like Stonewall.

The statement draws a conclusion that failing to support a partner's feelings about their gender is not equivalent to domestic abuse without providing sufficient evidence or reasoning to support this assertion.

cases.name: Americans' Views on COVID-19 Vaccine Side Effects

sentences.1: A recent survey has revealed that almost a quarter of Americans believe they know someone who died from side effects of the COVID-19 vaccine.
sentences.2: The survey found that 24% of American adults claim to know someone personally who died due to the side effects of the COVID-19 vaccine. In contrast, a significant 69% of respondents stated they don't know anyone who died from being vaccinated against the virus.
sentences.3: Even more people say they might be willing to become plaintiffs in a class-action lawsuit against vaccine makers.
sentences.4: Furthermore, the survey delved into the potential legal ramifications of these beliefs.
sentences.5: A notable 42% of respondents expressed that they would 'likely' join a major class-action lawsuit against big pharma if one were to file a lawsuit concerning vaccine side effects. This includes 24% who said it's 'very likely' they'd join such a lawsuit.
sentences.6: On the other hand, 47% of those surveyed 'aren't likely' to join a class-action lawsuit against vaccine makers, with 25% stating it's 'not at all likely' they would participate. An additional 11% remain uncertain.
sentences.7: The survey also highlighted some demographic differences. For instance, more men (51%) than women (44%) claim to know someone who died from vaccine side effects. Adults under 40 are less likely to know someone who died from the virus but are more inclined to join a lawsuit against pharmaceutical companies for vaccine side effects. Interestingly, men under 40 are particularly likely to say they'd join a class-action lawsuit. Racial differences were also evident in the survey results. While 43% of white respondents said they know someone who died from the COVID-19 virus, this number rises to 52% for black respondents and 57% for other minorities. However, fewer whites (20%) than blacks (28%) or other minorities (32%) claim to know someone who died from vaccine side effects. Black respondents were found to be more willing to join a class-action lawsuit for vaccine side effects.

Explanation.explanation: The survey delves into the potential legal ramifications of beliefs regarding vaccine side effects but does not provide evidence or support for the likelihood of these outcomes.

The survey data highlights demographic differences in knowing someone who died from the COVID-19 virus and willingness to join a class-action lawsuit for vaccine side effects. However, it incorrectly implies a causal relationship between race and the likelihood of knowing someone who died from vaccine side effects and willingness to join a lawsuit.

cases.name: Elon Musk's Warning About WW3

sentences.1: X owner Elon Musk warned on Monday that the world appears to be 'sleepwalking into World War Three' and will soon pass the point of no return.
sentences.2: During a recent X 'spaces' discussion with GOP presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, Musk said: 'I think we are sleepwalking our way into World War Three with one foolish decision after another, and people should be deeply self-reflective if their predictions have not come true, they should consider whether perhaps their other predictions may not come true either. I mean, what is the track record here? It's not good.'
sentences.3: Infowars.com reports: Musk appeared to be referring to world leaders like Joe Biden who makes 'one foolish decision after another,' and was questioning predictions made by other establishment politicians and media talking heads.
sentences.4: The tech billionaire also questioned how humanity can work together to avoid the 'civilizational risk' of a third world war and suggested we prioritize promoting peace.
sentences.5: Speaking more about the prospect of a global fight, Musk emphasized the threat posed to the West if Iran, China and Russia were to join forces militarily.

sentences.8: Newly independent news anchor Tucker Carlson similarly issued a warning about the threat of America being dragged into war during a Monday video release.

Explanation.explanation: Elon Musk is a tech billionaire and entrepreneur, not a political analyst or foreign policy expert, so his critique of world leaders like Joe Biden may lack the necessary expertise in geopolitics.
Tucker Carlson's warning about America being dragged into war may be seen as a premature or unwarranted conclusion without providing sufficient evidence or context.

cases.name: Bipartisan House Lawmakers Are Demanding That Biden Drops Julian Assange Case

sentences.1: House members from opposing sides of the aisle have joined forces in demanding that the Biden administration drop its case against Julian Assange.
sentences.2: The two congressmen have asked fellow House members to join their bipartisan attempt urging the Biden administration to withdraw the US extradition request.
sentences.3: According to Fox News, Massie's and McGovern's letter to fellow House members notes Assange's case represents an attack on press freedom.

Explanation.explanation: The argument appeals to tradition by highlighting the concerns expressed by international media outlets, human rights advocates, and members of Congress as a basis for supporting the withdrawal of the extradition request. This fallacy assumes that because past opinions have been against Assange's prosecution, it is the right course of action.

The conclusion drawn that Assange's case represents an attack on press freedom may be questioned due to the varying perspectives on the matter. While some argue for press freedom, others may view Assange's actions as violating national security laws rather than a pure exercise of press freedom.

sentences.1: In typically dramatic fashion, Santos announced his run while President Joe Biden delivered his State of the Union speech.

cases.name: Disaster for Trump as Truth Social Crashes at Critical SOTU Moment

sentences.1: Donald Trump may have rage-posted his way through President Joe Biden's State of the Union address on Truth Social, but his social media site crashed for many before Biden even entered the House chamber, with technical issues lingering for at least an hour before and into his remarks.
sentences.2: Beginning shortly before 9 p.m. EST Thursday, outages numbered in the thousands, according to Downdetector.
sentences.3: The outages peaked an hour later and then began to slowly resume back to normal, according to the monitor.
sentences.4: Around the same time, users on X reported not being able to access Trump's feed, with some—including former Trump White House Press Secretary Alyssa Farah Griffin—mocking him for it.
sentences.5: "Trump said he'd be live fact-checking Biden's SOTU but Truth Social appears to be down. Sad!" she wrote on X.
sentences.6: On Fox News, meanwhile, anchor Bret Baier—who had read out loud some of Trump's posts—invited him to just call in.
sentences.7: "If the former president wants to call in," Baier said, likely speaking directly to Trump through the screen, "we're happy to put him [on] instead of just reading Truth Social posts."
sentences.8: Those who were able to see what Trump had to say were likely not surprised, as his posts were largely negative reactions to people he saw on the broadcast.
sentences.9: "Thankfully, we don't have to be looking at RINO Mitt Romney much longer!" Trump wrote of the retiring Utah senator who has opposed Trump's 2024 candidacy.
sentences.10: Trump, who incited a mob of supporters that broke into the Capitol and House chamber on Jan. 6, 2021, then accused Biden of being "very disrespectful to our country" because his address in that same chamber didn't begin promptly at 9 p.m.
sentences.11: He also predictably took aim at Biden during his speech, insisting the president was "angry and crazy" and that "the words are not flowing smoothly out of his mouth!"

Explanation.explanation: Trump's comments on Mitt Romney and Biden focus on their character rather than their policies or actions.
Trump's remarks, such as calling Biden "angry and crazy," are attacks on the person rather than addressing the content of Biden's speech.
Accusations like Biden being "very disrespectful to our country" and "angry and crazy" play on emotional reactions rather than providing factual critique.
Trump's statements about Biden being "disrespectful" and "angry and crazy" lead to conclusions without substantial evidence.

cases.name: Can 'Kosher' Phones Used by Ultra-Orthodox Jews Cure Tech Addiction?

sentences.1: As an elder millennial, I received my first cell phone during my senior year of high school.
sentences.2: I still remember the novelty of finding out how easy and seamless it was to contact people and download apps.
sentences.3: Back then, no one fully understood how addictive these technologies were.
sentences.4: Today, smartphone addiction is widely acknowledged, and most people I know are actively seeking to minimize screen time and shield their children from the highly addictive nature of technology.
sentences.5: However, across the world, ultra-orthodox Jews have consistently refrained from adopting smartphones as a community and maintain a cautious approach to internet usage.
sentences.6: Ultra-orthodox groups are relatively secluded and are characterized by their strict adherence to Jewish law, particularly those concentrated in Israel and America but also found in various countries such as Australia, Canada, and England.
sentences.7: They have chosen to eschew the internet and smartphones, and perceive these technologies as excessively addictive and incongruent with their traditional way of life.
sentences.8: "I am a native New Yorker, but I saw zero footage of September 11th," Frieda Vizel told The Daily Beast.
sentences.9: She's a 39-year-old woman who grew up as part of New York's ultra-orthodox Satmar community but chose to leave that way of life more than a decade ago.
sentences.10: "The footage was completely inaccessible to me [in my community]."
sentences.11: She grew up in the Hasidic Jewish town of Kiryas Joel in upstate New York, where she had no access to screens or television.
sentences.12: The resistance to embrace smart technologies unfolded gradually.
sentences.13: During the early 2000s, with technological advancements, some within the ultra-orthodox community began to buy some of the earliest versions of smartphones like Blackberries.
sentences.14: Vizel, who runs a popular YouTube channel that explains many aspects of ultra-orthodox Jewish life and works as a tour guide for people who are curious about Hasidic Jews in New York, remembers this early period clearly.
sentences.15: "After I got married [in the early 2000s], I had a mobile phone.
sentences.16: Everyone in the community bought one," she recalled.
sentences.17: The technology was rapidly gaining popularity and was eagerly adopted.
sentences.18: However, the rabbis soon realized that smartphones, with their swiftly advancing features and fast internet speed, would be challenging to control and could jeopardize the community's way of life.
sentences.19: To counter this risk, smartphones were prohibited, and a novel approach emerged: "kosher" phones.
sentences.20: Kosher phones, often endorsed by rabbis for community use, typically come in two varieties.
sentences.21: They can be extremely simple phones with minimal features, like basic calling and no internet, while others are smart devices retrofitted with filters that can be updated and installed by designated individuals within the ultra-orthodox community at the time of purchase.
sentences.22: These filters guarantee that no distractions or apps conflicting with the expectations of the ultra-orthodox lifestyle are allowed.
sentences.23: While pornographic websites are obviously blocked, other more innocuous websites like YouTube or apps like Spotify may also be limited due their perceived incompatibility.
sentences.24: Filters are adaptable and can be modified upon special request to include apps or browser access necessary for business or school purposes.
sentences.25: "When I first heard about them, I started to think, 'Is this going to catch on?
sentences.26: Are they going to get people to turn in their smartphones and get people to buy these basic phones?'" said Vizel.
sentences.27: A quick walk around any ultra-orthodox Jewish enclave anywhere in the world will show that the ban on smartphones has been remarkably successful.
sentences.28: "It is mind boggling to me to see the rate of success.
sentences.29: In Hasidic Williamsburg, you see kosher phones everywhere and you rarely see a smartphone," Vizel said.
sentences.30: "I watched this happen in real time, and I thought it was impossible."
sentences.31: In contrast to the ubiquitous online presence in today's hyper-connected world, the ultra-orthodox community follows a different approach.
sentences.32: Adults may have access to internet-enabled devices for work or study, albeit with limitations and filters and they are not online all the time.
sentences.33: Access is never granted to children under the age of 18.
sentences.34: "There is an acceptance that smartphones and the internet are necessary," Vizel said.
sentences.35: However, they "try not to bring it into their life," and don't subscribe to "hyper-addicting smartphone culture."
sentences.36: Interestingly, Vizel finds that she is often recognized and spotted by members of her former community, who have clearly been watching her videos on YouTube, perhaps with a filter like KosherTube, which ensures content that is viewable and appropriate for members of an ultra-orthodox Jewish community.
sentences.37: "I have a ton of viewers on my YouTube channel who are Hasidic," she said.
sentences.38: "But many don't have smartphones."
sentences.39: Even though kosher phones are widely used in ultra-orthodox communities, it does not necessarily result in lower levels of addiction.
sentences.40: Technology can prove to be incredibly enticing even with the filters and limited features.
sentences.41: "People can call hotlines and listen to the news, and people are enamoured by that," Vizel said.
sentences.42: "One of the ubiquitous sights in Williamsburg is that there are people glued to their phones. [...] Kosher phones are addictive but in a different way."
sentences.43: Imposing restrictions on internet access also has its drawbacks.
sentences.44: Leah Boulton is the founder and CEO of Pathways Melbourne, a group dedicated to supporting and empowering ultra-Orthodox Jews who are questioning their lifestyle, practices and beliefs.
sentences.45: She told The Daily Beast that there are multiple challenges created by the technology.
sentences.46: For one, the use of kosher phones can complicate the process of challenging their beliefs, as filters may block access to supportive websites and hinder the acquisition of essential information.
sentences.47: "Often when we start engaging with people, they have managed to access some form of internet," she said.
sentences.48: "Last year, we had a young man with two sim cards.
sentences.49: He had a kosher and non-kosher one.
sentences.50: It was very hard to contact him."
sentences.51: Boulton doesn't criticize anyone who uses a kosher phone.
sentences.53: However, it does lead to a more limited worldview.
sentences.54: "And this controls the risks that may lead to questioning."
sentences.56: While imposing restrictions on oneself and family members can provide a sense of manageability for mobile phone users, issues arise when there is a need for broader access to the world, making kosher phones a significant concern.
sentences.57: "If a child or adult is in an unsafe family environment, kosher phones allow little means to see that what they are experiencing is unacceptable," Boulton explained.
sentences.58: Despite some of the drawbacks, adopting a simpler lifestyle with a kosher phone still triggers a yearning for Vizelâ€”especially when she sees ultra-orthodox children enjoying life without being tethered to an iPad or smartphone.
sentences.59: "The community's success in keeping kids off social media and off the internet is predicated on all of them being in the same situation," she said.
sentences.60: "If your kid is bored there are other children [who are] bored and want to play with them.

Explanation.explanation: The argument implies that refraining from adopting smartphones is justified because it's an ingrained tradition in the ultra-orthodox community.
The rabbis' decision to prohibit smartphones and introduce kosher phones relies on the traditional values of the community.
The text concludes that the ban on smartphones in ultra-orthodox Jewish enclaves has been remarkably successful without providing concrete evidence or data to support this claim.

cases.name: Monolingual Trump Slams Migrants Who 'Don't Speak Languages'

sentences.1: Monolingual former President Donald Trump lashed out Thursday at immigrants to the United States who, as he put it, 'don't speak languages.'
sentences.2: While speaking at the U.S.-Mexico border in Eagle Pass, Texas—the same day that President Joe Biden visited the border in Brownsville—Trump echoed his increasingly angry and pessimistic approach to describing immigration to the United States.
sentences.3: 'They're coming from jails, and they're coming from prisons, and they're coming from mental institutions, and they're coming from insane asylums, and they're terrorists. They're being let into our country, and it's horrible,' said Trump, who not that long ago declared that those same people are 'poisoning the blood of our country.'
sentences.4: Trump then claimed that no one has given him a satisfactory answer on the topic.
sentences.5: 'Nobody can explain to me how allowing millions of people from places unknown, from countries unknown, who don't speak languages—we have languages coming into our country—we have nobody that even speaks those languages. They're truly foreign languages. Nobody speaks them,' he said. 'And they're pouring into our country, and they're bringing with them tremendous problems, including medical problems, as you know.'
sentences.6: CNN, which aired a portion of Trump's comments, cut away for a fact-check minutes later by reporter Daniel Dale, an editorial strategy that is becoming more prevalent among major news networks.
sentences.7: 'I asked the Trump campaign: what is the evidence that unnamed foreign leaders are emptying out their institutions, their jails, sending people here as migrants? They couldn't come up with anything,' Dale told anchor Kaitlan Collins.
sentences.8: Dale also addressed Trump's dismissive comments about languages.
sentences.9: 'He told the story that he's told before, Kaitlan, about people arriving speaking languages that no one's ever heard. He said in a previous, recent speech [that] we didn't even have one translator who could understand this language,' Dale said. 'This, I've looked into this; it seems to be just conjured out of thin air. It's nonsense.'

Explanation.explanation: Trump uses emotionally charged language to evoke fear and anger about immigrants, describing them as criminals and terrorists without addressing the actual issues.
Trump selectively highlights negative aspects of immigrants, such as their inability to speak English and alleged medical problems, while ignoring positive contributions and success stories.
Trump makes a broad generalization about immigrants, claiming they are all criminals or mentally ill, based on a few extreme examples.
Trump makes a claim about the negative impact of immigrants without providing concrete evidence to support his assertions.

cases.name: Trump's Appeal Could Be Short-Lived for a Simple Reason

sentences.1: The massive bank fraud judgment issued against Trump in New York was written in a very particular way that could quickly disappoint Trump.
sentences.2: Donald Trump is working hard to get an appeal of the $464 million judgment levied against him for committing bank fraud.
sentences.3: But if he does fork over the cash and get that appeal, he may find that it doesn't take the higher courts long to swat it down.
sentences.4: That's because the 92-page opinion issued by New York Supreme Court Justice Arthur F. Engoron was tailor-made to withstand appeal—and give the state's First Judicial Department a roadmap to uphold the decision.
sentences.5: "The reason why this opinion is so long and so specific is to emphasize to the appellate court how much care the judge took in issuing this decision," said Jennifer B. Arlin, an expert on appeals who teaches legal writing at Brooklyn Law School.
sentences.6: A review of the judgment demonstrates that it was structured in an unusual format, one that dedicates a disproportionate amount of space to analyzing the facts presented during the 11-week trial—and provides a simple guide for an appellate court to quickly examine it, understand the judge's reasoning process, and come to a swift decision.
sentences.7: "It's so well laid out that it says, 'Go ahead—challenge me,'" said Diane Peress, a former prosecutor who now teaches at John Jay College of Criminal Justice.
sentences.8: "I think it's very smartly done, because it really shows that he didn't just say, 'Hey, half a billion dollars, whatever.' It shows that he based it on fact, on law."
sentences.9: All court orders lay out what are called "findings of fact" and "conclusions of law," a combination that explains how and why a judge issued a decision.
sentences.10: For example, Colorado Judge Sarah B. Wallace's "findings of fact" took up exactly a third of her November order that concluded Trump engaged in insurrection but should be kept on the 2024 ballot—an order that was later overturned and is now under consideration by the Supreme Court.
sentences.11: By contrast, Engoron's "findings of fact" about Trump's bank fraud stretch on for 68 pages, taking up more than two-thirds of this opinion.
sentences.12: In that space, the court lists 39 witnesses, explaining their testimony in detail and even offering acerbic commentary about their credibility.
sentences.13: Engoron's order particularly tears apart the integrity of former Trump Organization controller Jeffrey McConney, noting how "he obfuscated and equivocated at length before finally conceding" details about his role in the ploy to shed blame over to outside accountants for lying to banks.
sentences.14: The judge's decision also notes how a tenured professor at New York University clocked $877,500 to offer expert testimony about financial accounting—only to ignore "numerous significant errors" in Trump's personal financial statements, repeating the "unpersuasive" performance he gave at another major trial involving the oil giant Exxon Mobil.
sentences.15: "By doggedly attempting to justify every misstatement, Professor Bartov lost all credibility in the eyes of the court," the order says.
sentences.16: That means appellate judges can get a clear sense of the trial by reading through Engoron's retelling—without having to peruse the 6,758-page trial transcript.
sentences.17: They can rely on the observations of Engoron and his law clerk, Allison Greenfield, who sat by the judge during the entire trial.
sentences.18: "This court listened carefully to every witness, every question, every answer.
sentences.19: Witnesses testified from the witness stand, approximately a yard from the court, who was thus able to observe expressions, demeanor, and body language.
sentences.20: The court has also considered the simple touchstones of self-interest and other motives, common sense, and overall veracity," Engoron's order says.
sentences.21: This laser-like focus on the witnesses and their reliability is actually a conscious and meticulous effort to build a case that will stand up on appeal, legal scholars said.
sentences.22: Arlin noted that appellate courts will look at the order through a specific lens called the standard of review.
sentences.23: Higher court judges can thoroughly examine Engoron's legal conclusions, but they have to defer to his findings of fact—particularly when the trial was his decision and his alone.
sentences.24: There was no jury; Trump never asked for one formally.
sentences.25: "The very detailed listings of the 'findings of fact' are on purpose," Arlin said.
sentences.26: "The trial court is in a unique position to not only hear the testimony and look at the evidence, but as he said very explicitly, he was able to see the facial expressions and attitudes and eye contact."
sentences.27: "He went out of his way to say he was just a few feet away when they were testifying.
sentences.28: He's the judge of the credibility of the witnesses," Arlin continued.
sentences.29: "The appellate courts have to rely on the trial court's assessment of credibility, and that was a huge issue in this case.
sentences.30: He found that these people were clearly lying and lacked credibility."
sentences.31: While it's normal for judges to cite witness testimony, it's exceedingly rare for a court's order to provide a list of Dramatis Personae and comb through their statements.
sentences.32: Engoron's order listed all but one of the entire trial's 40 witnesses.
sentences.33: The court took 37 days to issue the judgment after closing arguments in January.
sentences.34: "It is unusual, yes.
sentences.35: But we're dealing with an unusual defendant and the armies of lawyers he's going to employ who are going to leave no stone unturned," Peress said, stressing that Engoron is "trying to make it bulletproof."
sentences.36: An appellate court can only overturn Engoron's fact findings if he was in what's deemed "clear error," hence the more detailed approach to listing every aspect of the case.
sentences.37: The judgment also reviewed 10 different Trump properties and the fraud that took place in each one, and separately examined eight instances of fraud.
sentences.38: The next move in this chess game is Trump's to make.
sentences.39: First Judicial Department Judge Anil Singh on Wednesday temporarily stopped the bulk of Engoron's judgment, which submits the Trump Organization to severe scrutiny going forward, and ejects the fraudsters from the business world—including the real estate tycoon, his sons Don Jr. and Eric, and former company chief financial officer Allen Weisselberg.
sentences.40: But the appellate judge refused Trump's low-ball $100 million offer to stay the execution of the full judgment, meaning that New York Attorney General Letitia James next month could begin aggressively moving to seize his assets to satisfy the outstanding half-billion-dollar bill.
sentences.41: In mid-March, Engoron can greenlight the AG forcefully grabbing Trump brand properties and putting them up for auction.
sentences.42: It's looking increasingly likely that Trump will actually have to come up with the money anyway to stop that.
sentences.43: New York appellate bond rules require that he front 110 percent to 120 percent of the judgment, a massive sum he doesn't appear to have, especially now that he also owes $83 million for losing his second rape defamation case in January.
sentences.44: But legal observers are particularly interested in what happens if Trump continues with his appeal without trying to stay the execution of the judgment—an awkward scenario in which the AG seizes a Trump building or golf course even as he fights the legal battle in higher courts.
sentences.45: Either way, Trump faces a stark deadline in late March, just days before he starts his very first criminal trial against the Manhattan District Attorney on March 25.

Explanation.explanation: The argument relies heavily on the opinions of Jennifer B. Arlin and Diane Peress without establishing their expertise or relevance to the specific case.
The reference to the unusual defendant and armies of lawyers relies on Peress's authority without further evidence.

The argument suggests that the detailed judgment is inherently strong because it follows a traditional format of 'findings of fact' and 'conclusions of law,' without addressing the specific merits of the case.
The appeal to tradition is used to imply the thoroughness and reliability of the judgment without considering other potential flaws.

cases.name: Testy Exchange Between Hunter Biden, Matt Gaetz Revealed in Deposition Transcript

sentences.1: Rep. Matt Gaetz (R-FL) and Hunter Biden had a tense exchange Wednesday during the latter's testimony before the House Oversight Committee, with the president's son taking issue with Gaetz's line of questioning.
sentences.2: In the closed-door session, Biden called the impeachment probe into his father a 'partisan political pursuit' being pushed by 'MAGA-motivated conspiracies,' according to a transcript released by the committee Thursday.
sentences.3: Gaetz, a frequent defender of former President Donald Trump, questioned Biden about serving on the board of Burisma, a Ukrainian energy company.
sentences.4: Gaetz wanted to know if Biden, a recovering addict, was 'on drugs' while on the board.
sentences.5: Biden's lawyer, Abbe Lowell, first took issue with that.
sentences.6: 'One of the things that I spoke to staff that you just asked about as to whether it's outside the bounds.
sentences.7: If you want to spend the next part of the last hour you have asking about his drug use, go at it,' Lowell said.
sentences.8: 'It's outside the scope.
sentences.9: It certainly has no relevance to an impeachment inquiry nor does it have anything to do with oversight of ethics legislation that may address family members of presidents or vice presidents.
sentences.10: So go at it, but it's outside the scope and you're wasting your time.'
sentences.11: Gaetz then repeated his question to Biden: 'Were you on drugs when you were on the Burisma board?'
sentences.12: Biden replied: 'Mr. Gaetz, look me in the eye.
sentences.13: You really think that's appropriate to ask me?'
sentences.14: After Gaetz said it 'absolutely' was, Biden shot back: 'Of all the people sitting around this table, do you think that's appropriate to ask me?'
sentences.15: Biden may have been alluding to a series of salacious allegations against the Florida firebrand, including a Daily Beast report earlier this month revealing that in 2021 a young woman told prosecutors working on a sex trafficking investigation that she had sex with Gaetz at a party which she was paid to attend and where drugs were present.
sentences.16: When approached for comment at the time, a Gaetz spokesperson said: 'Rep. Gaetz does not know anything about the woman you're referencing.'
sentences.17: Last February, federal prosecutors decided to close that investigation into Gaetz without filing charges.
sentences.18: Gaetz is still facing an ongoing House Ethics Committee inquiry into allegations of sex crimes and drug use, among other things.
sentences.19: Gaetz has maintained that the inquiry is retaliation for his role in last year's ouster of House Speaker Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.20: 'The Ethics Committee is engaging in payback against me for ousting the person who singularly appointed every Republicanâ€”Kevin McCarthy,' he told ABC News earlier this month.
sentences.21: After Biden asked Gaetz whether his question was 'appropriate,' Gaetz replied, 'Yeah.
sentences.22: Are you going to answer it?'
sentences.23: After a little more back-and-forth, Biden responded at length.
sentences.24: 'I will answer it this way: I have been absolutely transparent about my drug use.
sentences.25: Again, I spoke to you all earlier this morning about that.
sentences.26: I'm sorry; I'm an addict.
sentences.27: I was an addict.
sentences.28: I have been in recovery for over four and a half years now, Mr. Gaetz.
sentences.29: I work really, really hard at it,' he said.
sentences.30: 'Let me answer.
sentences.31: I work really hard at it, under an enormous amount of pressure.
sentences.32: Was I an addict?
sentences.33: Yes, I was an addict.
sentences.34: What does that have to do with whether or not you're going to go forward with an impeachment of my father other than to simply try to embarrass me?'

Explanation.explanation: Gaetz's question about Biden's drug use is a personal attack to undermine his credibility instead of addressing the actual issue.
Bringing up allegations against Gaetz diverts attention from the actual topic of the questioning.
Gaetz's repeated questioning about drug use attacks Biden's character rather than his arguments or the situation at hand.
Biden's response evokes sympathy by discussing his struggles with addiction to shift focus from the impeachment inquiry.

cases.name: Trump Can't Stop Comparing Himself to Alexei Navalny During Fox News Town Hall

sentences.1: Having to pay a fine for bank fraud "is a form of Navalny," Trump said during a Fox News town hall Tuesday night.
sentences.2: Trump Can't Stop Comparing Himself to Alexei Navalny
sentences.3: Having to pay a fine for bank fraud "is a form of Navalny," Trump said during a Fox News town hall.
sentences.4: Donald Trump once again compared the death of Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny to his recent legal woes, this time during a primetime Fox News town hall.
sentences.5: Just a day after complaining on Truth Social that Navalny's death reminded him of "Radical Left Politicians, Prosecutors, and Judges leading us down a path to destruction" in part through "Grossly Unfair Courtroom Decisions," Trump had a similar reaction when host Laura Ingraham asked how he is going to pay up.
sentences.6: "It is a form of Navalny. It is a form of communism or fascism," Trump responded, before insulting the judge in his recently concluded New York business fraud case.
sentences.7: Judge Arthur Engoron ruled Friday that Trump is banned from operating a business in New York for three years and must pay a $364 million fine, plus interest.
sentences.8: Trump's two adult sons were also fined $4 million each (before interest) and are prohibited from running a New York business for two years.
sentences.9: The judgment in the civil fraud trial, which comes on the heels of a $83 million judgment levied after Trump lost a defamation case brought by writer E. Jean Carroll, forces Trump to put up the fine plus several million more if he wants to file an appeal.
sentences.10: When asked Tuesday if he would "give up" one of his properties for this purpose, Trump sidestepped the question, instead withdrawing from his jacket pocket a print-out of the Eighth Amendment and reading it aloud.
sentences.11: "'Excessive bail shall not be required, nor excessive fines imposed, nor cruel and unusual punishments inflicted,'" he quoted, after which Ingraham noted that the ruling came from a state court rather than a federal one.
sentences.12: The Fox host, reiterating that the amount is "such a huge amount of money," tried again.
sentences.13: "You have to decide whether you're going to put up that bond in escrow to appeal.
sentences.14: Are you going to do that?" she asked.
sentences.15: Trump, who is also barred from borrowing money at any New York bank for three years, didn't directly respond.
sentences.16: "I'll tell you what we're going to do.
sentences.17: Number one, we have a lot of cash.
sentences.18: But that doesn't mean he can take it," Trump said, presumably referring to Engoron.
sentences.19: The former president then went off topic by railing against President Joe Biden, leaving Ingraham's question unanswered.
sentences.20: Also during the town hall, Trump alluded to last year's $785 million defamation settlement that Fox News paid to Dominion Voting Systems due to false claims it aired about the 2020 election—suggesting that he would lay off his own debunked claims of widespread voter fraud due to the network's own complicated history with the subject matter.
sentences.21: After saying that he "did much better" in the 2020 election than four years prior, Trump explained that he wouldn't be going into detail.
sentences.22: "I won't get into it, because of Fox," he said.
sentences.23: At another point in the hour-long sit-down, the GOP frontrunner identified six possible running mates should he clinch the nomination.
sentences.24: After Ingraham mentioned Trump's former primary rivals Ron DeSantis, Tim Scott and Vivek Ramaswamy, as well as Florida Rep. Byron Donalds, South Dakota Gov. Kristi Noem and former Hawaii Democratic Rep. Tulsi Gabbard, Trump confirmed that all are on his shortlist.
sentences.25: "Honestly, all of those people are good," he said.
sentences.26: "They're all good, they're all solid."
sentences.27: Trump on Tuesday had especially nice things to say about Scott, who was in attendance at the South Carolina event ahead of that state's primary on Saturday.
sentences.28: "He's been such a great advocate," Trump said.
sentences.29: "I have to say this in a very positive way: Tim Scott, he has been much better for me than he was for himself."

Explanation.explanation: Comparing having to pay a fine for bank fraud to the persecution of Alexei Navalny is a faulty analogy because the two situations are not similar in relevant respects.

Trump's diversion to railing against President Joe Biden and discussing the Fox News defamation settlement when asked about paying the fine serves as a red herring, as it sidetracks the conversation from the original topic.

Appealing to the Eighth Amendment's clause on 'excessive fines' without addressing the specifics of why the fine is excessive in this context appeals to emotion, trying to evoke a sense of injustice without substantiating the claim.

Trump's claim that 'Radical Left Politicians, Prosecutors, and Judges' are leading to 'destruction' through 'Grossly Unfair Courtroom Decisions' misrepresents the actions and intentions of these individuals, constructing a strawman argument.

cases.name: Donald Trump's Cash Crunch Just Got Much, Much Worse

sentences.1: As Donald Trump's legal troubles consume more and more of his time, they're also consuming more of his donors' money and there's a huge hole in the bucket.
sentences.2: On Tuesday, Trump's 'Save America' leadership political action committee reported raising just $8,508 from donors in the entire month of January, while spending about $3.9 million, according to a new filing with the Federal Election Commission.
sentences.3: Nearly $3 million of that overall spending total was used for one purpose: to pay lawyers.
sentences.4: At the same time, the Trump campaign itself reported a net loss of more than $2.6 million for the month of January.
sentences.5: It raised about $8.8 million while spending around $11.5 million, according to a separate filing made public on Tuesday.
sentences.6: The filings reveal that Trump is continuing to burn through his donors' funds as he struggles to feed two massive cash drains astronomical legal bills stemming from numerous civil cases and four criminal indictments, plus the costs of a national presidential campaign.
sentences.7: After the Trump filings were released on Tuesday evening, his sole primary challenger, Nikki Haley, flashed a sign of strength, with her campaign reporting $11.5 million in receipts last month.
sentences.8: It is the first-ever fundraising period where Haley's campaign outraised Trump.
sentences.9: Despite reporting almost no donations in January, the Save America PAC a group Trump launched days after the 2020 election, ostensibly to fund legal challenges actually increased its bottom line by more than $1 million, ending the month with nearly $6.3 million on hand.
sentences.10: However, that increase can't be chalked up to new donations.
sentences.11: It's entirely due to a $5 million transfer from a different pro-Trump super PAC, which is still in the process of refunding $60 million that the former president demanded back last year, as his legal bills threatened to put Save America, his legal slush fund, into bankruptcy.
sentences.12: The super PAC has been kicking that refund back in $5 million installments beginning late last spring, but that emergency bailout won't last, either the full refund is set to be completed by June.
sentences.13: There's another metric for the depth of Trump's financial strain: Save America itself had to bail out yet another one of Trump's PACs, transferring $500,000 to his old campaign committee in the middle of January.
sentences.14: That group, called 'Make America Great Again PAC,' started the year with only about $570,000 in the bank, so the mid-month injection from the sputtering Save America suggests that MAGA PAC might very well be in danger of bottoming out too.
sentences.15: A Trump spokesperson didn't immediately respond to a comment request.
sentences.16: As he heads into his third consecutive presidential campaign, it's safe to say Trump's cash apparatus is complicated.
sentences.17: At this point, the Save America PAC exists almost exclusively to cover the former president's legal bills, but Trump also has to fund his political campaign.
sentences.18: He does that by raising the bulk of his money through a joint fundraising committee, which automatically splits the proceeds 90 percent goes to the campaign, with Save America cleaning up the other 10 percent, according to the terms of online solicitations.
sentences.19: Last month, however, the joint fundraising committee didn't send any money to Save America, the latest filings show, though it did transfer about $8.5 million to the Trump campaign.
sentences.20: This suggests Save America might still have as much as $850,000 headed its way from January fundraising efforts a drop in the bucket, considering the ferocious burn rate of those legal costs.
sentences.21: Trump's cash crunch is hitting at a terrible time.
sentences.22: Recent weeks have seen two massive legal judgments against the former president.
sentences.23: First came the $83.3 million sum for the writer E. Jean Carroll, whom he was found liable for sexually abusing and defaming; that was followed weeks later with a whopping $355 million fine for years of business fraud in New York.
sentences.24: Along with interest and other costs, those two rulings alone could set Trump back as much as $600 million.
sentences.25: While Trump is a billionaire, his choice to pass his legal costs on to his donors is threatening to derail the GOP's national fundraising efforts.
sentences.26: Trump is now attempting a takeover of the Republican National Committee, planting MAGA loyalists and even his own daughter-in-law at the top echelons of party leadership.
sentences.27: The Daily Beast previously reported that this self-interested maneuvering could severely constrain the RNC as the national party struggles to unify behind its beleaguered standard-bearer during a monumental election cycle.
sentences.28: But Trump can't raise money with the party until he officially secures the nomination, which could happen as soon as March.
sentences.29: And a breakdown of the Trump campaign's spending last month shows that the primary contest is taking its toll, even as that competition winnowed to just Haley.
sentences.30: The campaign's biggest January line item was the nearly $4.7 million spent for placed media, which accounts for TV ad spending.
sentences.31: Another roughly $820,000 went out the door for audio visual support at events, $602,000 for video production, nearly $550,000 in travel-related expenses, and more than $450,000 for polling services.
sentences.32: The campaign also shelled out about $15,000 for teleprompter services, a sharp increase over recent months, as Trump held rallies to bolster support as primary voting got underway.
sentences.33: Outside of those direct political costs, however, the campaign's biggest expense was the $830,000 it also dropped on lawyers.

Explanation.explanation: The article highlights Nikki Haley's fundraising success without considering the overall context of the campaign or other candidates.
The article uses the threat to national GOP fundraising to evoke concern about Trump's actions, appealing to the reader's emotions rather than presenting a logical argument.

cases.name: Kari Lake Comes Up Empty-Handed When Pressed About Arizona Election Claims

sentences.1: When it comes to Kari Lake's debunked theory of widespread election fraud in her 2022 Arizona gubernatorial race, she's not even sure 'who exactly stole the election,' she admitted Monday.
sentences.2: During an interview on Arizona's KTAR News 92.3 FM, Lake's false claims were challenged by the station's legal analyst, Barry Markson.
sentences.3: My question is, as you've been saying for three years, or for two years: can you tell us who stole the election from you and how they did it, and if you can't or you don't want to, that's OK, but I want to make sure the question is there in front of you,' Markso said.
sentences.4: A post-election lawsuit from Lake alleging election fraud was rejected in December 2022, with an Arizona court ruling that there was no 'clear and convincing evidence' the race outcome was affected by fraud.
sentences.5: Lake's additional legal losses extended through late last year. But that hasn't seemed to deter her.
sentences.6: 'I don't know who exactly stole the election,' Lake said, 'but there are a lot of people who are running elections poorly, and we've seen the result.'
sentences.7: A candidate for Senate in Arizona this year, Lake added: 'The elections are run poorly. They're run very poorly, and I don't know who exactly.'
sentences.8: At another point in the interview, Lake tried to explain critical comments she made in 2022 about former Arizona Sen. John McCain and his supporters.
sentences.9: But McCain's daughter, Megan, hasn't bought that Lake's remarks were made in jest.
sentences.10: 'Guess she realized she can't become a Senator without us,' McCain wrote on X Tuesday.

Explanation.explanation: Kari Lake claims election fraud but provides no evidence to support her assertion.
Lake diverts the attention from providing evidence of fraud to criticizing the way elections are run.
Megan McCain's comment focuses on Lake's character and aspirations rather than addressing the argument or claims Lake made.

cases.name: Roger Stone Caught on Tape Discussing Trump's Plan to Challenge 2024 Election

sentences.1: Self-proclaimed 'dirty trickster' Roger Stone was secretly videotaped at Mar-a-Lago during a remarkably candid conversation.
sentences.2: Roger Stone, a longtime Republican operative who served as an adviser to Donald Trump, was secretly recorded at Mar-a-Lago spilling the beans on the former president's strategy to challenge the results of the 2024 election should he lose again.
sentences.3: The self-described 'dirty trickster' of right-wing politics unknowingly divulged the plan to liberal reporters Lauren Windsor and Ally Sammarco, who posed as Trump fans and covertly videotaped him at a 'Catholics Prayer for Trump' event on March 19.
sentences.4: The recordings were first reported by Rolling Stone.
sentences.5: The remarkably candid conversation is just the latest released by Windsor and her left-leaning sting group, The Undercurrent, in recent weeks—and comes on the heels of headline-grabbing tapes that captured both Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito and his wife, Martha-Ann Alito, weighing in on a number of hot button culture war issues facing the court and the country.
sentences.6: Stone, who was a key figure in Trump's 'Stop the Steal' efforts following the 2020 election, characterized his plan to challenge election results in 2024 with three pillars: 'Lawyers, judges, technology.'
sentences.7: He also bragged that the Trump campaign occupied strong 'offensive footing' this time around.
sentences.8: 'In some states, it'll be easier to stop.
sentences.9: In other places it won't,' Stone told Sammarco.
sentences.10: 'At least this time when they do it, you have a lawyer and a judge, his home phone number standing by so you can stop it,' apparently referring to the certification of 2024 results.
sentences.11: 'We made no preparations last time, none,' he added.
sentences.12: Stone also tacitly endorsed storming the Capitol building after Sammarco told him she was at the insurrection.
sentences.13: 'That may not be necessary,' Stone continued.
sentences.14: 'There are technical, legal steps we have to take to try to have a more honest election.'
sentences.15: Stone noted during the conversation that the Trump campaign is attempting to change state voting laws and plans to immediately file a number of lawsuits seeking to change the results should the former president lose again, as Trump allies did in Michigan and several other states in 2020.
sentences.16: 'We should be suing in a half a dozen places,' Stone said of the Michigan lawsuit, adding that the RNC's war chest would be tapped to fund the various lawsuits.
sentences.17: The Trump campaign launched 62 lawsuits contesting the results of the election across the country in 2020.
sentences.18: However, most were quickly dismissed or dropped due to a lack of standing or evidence, according to Bloomberg Law.
sentences.19: Stone told Windsor that the Trump campaign even has governors who are ready to contest this November's election results—though he qualified, candidly, that there 'aren't many' willing to put their reputation on the line in service of the former president.

Explanation.explanation: The sentence mentions headline-grabbing tapes of Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito and his wife weighing in on culture war issues, which could be seen as invoking the authority of a Supreme Court Justice in an unrelated context to bolster the significance of the tapes.
These sentences discuss the number of lawsuits launched by the Trump campaign in 2020 and their outcomes, which sidetracks from the main topic of Stone's discussion about the 2024 election strategy.
The sentence refers to storming the Capitol building, which evokes strong emotional responses related to the events of January 6, 2021, rather than providing a logical argument.

cases.name: Jimmy Kimmel Fires Back at 'Preposterous' George Santos Lawsuit

sentences.1: After returning from what he described as an 'eventful' holiday weekend, Jimmy Kimmel on Tuesday had one question at the top of his mind: 'Did anyone else get sued by George Santos this weekend?'
sentences.2: More than two months after Kimmel, using a bevy of pseudonyms, got George Santos to record all sorts of bizarre Cameo videos—which the late-night host then promptly shared with viewers—the disgraced former congressman is now suing Kimmel, ABC, and Disney (the network's parent company) over the prank.
sentences.3: 'I am currently embroiled in the most preposterous lawsuit of all time,' Kimmel shared.
sentences.4: 'George Santos—a man Republicans kicked out of congress for being a fraud—is suing me for fraud!'
sentences.5: Which the host thinks is quite rude, frankly, 'because we did a nice thing.
sentences.6: We supported him by ordering his Cameo videos.'
sentences.7: Among the 'absolutely ridiculous messages' Kimmel sent to Santos via Cameo were congratulations—and well wishes—for 'Gary Fortuna for winning the Clearwater Florida Beef Eating Contest' by eating a record-breaking six pounds of ground beef in less than 30 minutes and promptly being hospitalized, and further congrats for Brenda 'on the successful cloning of her beloved schnauzer Adolf.'
sentences.8: Santos' reaction to the unexpected publicity was to demand an additional $20,000 from Kimmel for sharing the videos, but Kimmel made it clear he wasn't about to roll over for the man sometimes known as George Devolder.
sentences.9: And Kimmel's opinion on the matter—which has now escalated to a request for $750,000 plus damages—does not seem to have changed.
sentences.10: 'He says we deceived him under the guise of fandom soliciting personalized videos, only to then broadcast these on national television,' Kimmel explained.
sentences.11: 'And if there's one thing George Santos won't stand for, it's using a fake name under false pretenses.'
sentences.12: 'He says he thought these were real messages and he was duped,' Kimmel added of his video requests, noting that the serial fabulist is 'being represented by the prestigious law firm of Pot, Kettle, and Black.'
sentences.13: 'This is like being sued for paternity by Nick Cannon,' Kimmel concluded.

Explanation.explanation: Kimmel attacks Santos' character by pointing out that he was kicked out of Congress for fraud, rather than addressing the legitimacy of the lawsuit.
Kimmel distracts from the issue of whether he deceived Santos by highlighting the irony of Santos' own history of deception.
Kimmel compares being sued by Santos to being sued for paternity by Nick Cannon, which is a misleading analogy as these situations are not sufficiently similar.

sentences.17: Timberlake, who is in the middle of his "The Forget Tomorrow World Tour," told police he was following his friends home.
sentences.18: The Grammy winner's next court date is scheduled for July 26.
sentences.19: On Wednesday, Burke's office said the prominent lawyer "looks forward to vigorously defending Mr. Timberlake against these allegations."
sentences.20: "He will have a lot to say at the appropriate time," they said.
sentences.21: "He is currently awaiting full discovery from the DA's office."

sentences.23: When the man returned, the Post reports, the songwriter was downing his beverage.
sentences.24: The observer recalled: "The guy goes, 'Justin, that's my drink!'"
sentences.25: Meanwhile, the American Hotel's owner says Timberlake is welcome back anytime.
sentences.26: Ted Conklin told TMZ the former boy-band heartthrob was a "great guest and a nice guy" and insisted that he was not over-served at the establishment.

Explanation.explanation: The argument relies on an insider's statement to confirm the strength of the martini without providing solid evidence.
The blog's claim about the martini's alcohol level is used as evidence without verifying the credibility of the source.
The witness's claim that Timberlake appeared 'wasted' and took another patron's drink is used to evoke a negative emotional response without addressing the legal specifics of the case.

cases.name: How the NFL's 'Worst-Ever' Owner is Blocking Movie Showing 'Rapist' Trump

sentences.1: Former Washington Commanders owner Dan Snyder might be able to stop "The Apprentice" from hitting screens thanks to a bizarre twist: He helped finance the movie.

cases.name: Officials Livid With Climate Protesters Who Sprayed Stonehenge Orange

sentences.4: In contrast, he said, "the damage that is being done to all of our communities by oil and gas executives and the politicians that they've bought is going to run on for many generations."
sentences.5: During the appearance, Skeet challenged listeners with a question: "What is it that's more shocking—is it a bit of cornstarch on a treasured monument, or is it the fact that governments have admitted to burning more oil, gas, and coal when we're just coming off the back of 12 straight months of record temperatures that are leading to fires, floods, crop failures worldwide?"
sentences.6: The damage from climate inaction, Skeet said, is "going to lead to millions of people killed and displaced in the years to come."
sentences.7: Still, authorities and online spectators are about as livid as one might expect.
sentences.8: Prime Minister Rishi Sunak called the action a "disgraceful act of vandalism," according to NBC News.
sentences.9: Sunak echoed the sentiment on X, where he called Just Stop Oil "a disgrace."
sentences.10: Meanwhile, curators for English Heritage—which manages Stonehenge as a UNESCO World Heritage Site—are investigating the damage and called the decoration "extremely upsetting."
sentences.11: The site remains open to the public.
sentences.12: X is replete with negative reactions as well.
sentences.13: As one commenter put it, "I'm kind of with you on your campaign.
sentences.14: But this? This doesn't work.
sentences.15: This doesn't get people on side.
sentences.16: It does the opposite.
sentences.17: It's vandalism."
sentences.18: Speaking on PoliticsJOE, Skeet emphasized that the demonstration has successfully placed the climate crisis at the top of the world news cycle, where it would not have been before.
sentences.19: As for whether or not actions like this endear people to Just Stop Oil itself, he suggested that the question might be beside the point.
sentences.20: "There's ample research on this that suggest that though people don't like Just Stop Oil, they tend to actually disassociate it from the issue itself," Skeet said.
sentences.21: "So, generally, people will be going, 'Oh, I don't like these Just Stop Oil folks, but actually, the issue of the climate crisis is really important, and something needs to happen about it."
sentences.22: The protesters themselves are equally adamant that something must be done.
sentences.23: Niamh Lynch, a 21-year-old student from Oxford, said in Just Stop Oil's press release, "It's time for us to think about what our civilization will leave behind—what is our legacy? ...
sentences.24: Standing inert for generations works well for stones—not climate policy."
sentences.25: Rajan Naidu, a 73-year-old from Birmingham, added, "Either we end the fossil fuel era, or the fossil fuel era will end us."

Explanation.explanation: Skeet's statement about millions of people being killed and displaced leverages emotional impact to support his argument.
Niamh Lynch's statement evokes the concept of legacy and the emotional attachment to what civilization leaves behind.
Rajan Naidu's statement uses a dramatic comparison to the end of an era, invoking fear and urgency to persuade.
Skeet's question about what is more shocking between cornstarch on a monument and government actions sidetracks from discussing the specific action of vandalizing Stonehenge.
Skeet's question about comparing cornstarch on a monument to government actions distorts the argument by misrepresenting the significance of the act of vandalism.

sentences.5: Hannity backed the idea that Biden should be drug-tested, and Kimmel was happy to call his bluff: "Let's do it. Let's test the president for caffeine. Let's test Trump for Adderall and Cialis. Let's see how the tests come out."

sentences.7: "I mean, who in the world is buying this idea that there's some magic debate pill you can takeâ€¦ It's all nuts. It's just all nuttiness."

Kimmel introduces the idea of drug-testing Trump for Adderall and Cialis, which diverts attention from the main issue of the debate performance.
Kimmel uses emotive language by calling the idea of a 'magic debate pill' nuts, aiming to evoke ridicule rather than provide a rational argument.

cases.name: Biden Brutally Goes After Trump During State of the Union—Just Not by Name

sentences.1: Biden didn't shy away from attacking Trump or Republicans. But he did shy away from saying Trump's name.
sentences.2: In what could be his final State of the Union address, President Joe Biden poked and prodded Republicans on a number of issues—Ukraine, abortion, the border, even Jan. 6—contrasting GOP apathy with Democratic action as the general election campaign began in earnest Thursday night.
sentences.3: It was an unapologetically political speech, with Biden punching Republicans and Republicans punching right back. But Biden saved his sharpest contrasts, his most direct swipes, for the one Republican whose name he refused to mention: Donald Trump.
sentences.4: Biden repeatedly referenced Trump with titles like 'my predecessor' and 'the former Republican President,' avoiding his name throughout the entire speech even as he called Trump out repeatedly.
sentences.5: Just a few minutes into his address Thursday night, Biden noted that Trump had told Russian President Vladimir Putin to 'do whatever the hell you want' with respect to Ukraine.
sentences.6: 'A former American president actually said that, bowing down to a Russian leader,' Biden said. 'It's outrageous. It's dangerous. It's unacceptable.'
sentences.7: But Biden was just getting started with his criticism of Trump.
sentences.8: He dinged 'my predecessor'—as well as 'some of you here'—for seeking to 'bury the truth' about Jan. 6. 'I will not do that,' Biden said. 'This is a moment to speak the truth and bury the lies.'
sentences.9: He attacked 'my predecessor' for trying to overturn Roe v. Wade. 'He's the reason it was overturned. In fact, he brags about it,' Biden said.
sentences.10: He called out 'my predecessor' for his record on COVID and causing a 'mental health crisis of isolation and loneliness.' Biden said Trump 'failed the most basic duty'—'the duty to care.'
sentences.11: He went on to accuse 'my predecessor' of not buying American, of trying to take away health insurance for Americans, and of demanding that Republicans block a bipartisan border bill.
sentences.12: Biden's constant calls back to 'my predecessor' served multiple purposes. He was able to get overtly political without directly—by name—attacking Trump. But Biden also subtly connected the former president to the past, not the future, as both men argue about their age, ability, and record.
sentences.13: It was the topic of immigration, however, where Biden delivered his most relentless attacks on Trump and Republicans. He accused the GOP of 'playing politics' with border security so they could preserve immigration as a campaign issue for Trump.
sentences.14: 'I'm told my predecessor called Republicans in Congress and demanded they block the bill,' Biden said. 'He feels it would be a political win for me and a political loser for him.'
sentences.15: At another point, Biden contrasted himself with 'my predecessor' for offering a comprehensive immigration plan and making good on a bipartisan proposal to 'secure the border.'
sentences.16: Ever since Republicans followed Trump's orders to reject the bipartisan border security deal, Democrats have taken a more aggressive immigration posture on the campaign trail. They've made a sport out of labeling Republicans hypocrites for opposing a compromise bill they previously claimed was critical to addressing the 'crisis at the border.'
sentences.17: Biden was so aggressive on immigration that he even went toe-to-toe with one of the most predictable troublemakers in Congress: Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-GA). In a testy, unscripted exchange, Biden responded to Greene—who was violating House rules by wearing a MAGA hat on the House floor—as she demanded Biden acknowledge Laken Riley, a 22-year-old nursing student who police say was murdered by an undocumented immigrant.
sentences.18: Biden called Riley 'an innocent young woman who was killed.' And Biden adopted—either intentionally or not—GOP rhetoric on immigrants as he referred to Riley's killer as 'an illegal.'
sentences.19: While he certainly didn't score any points with progressives for that dehumanizing term, he did seem to neutralize a Republican talking point about his refusal to address the murder.
sentences.20: Overall, however, this was a speech for Democrats. Biden used the State of the Union as an opportunity to run through Democratic accomplishments during the first years of his presidency, like an infrastructure bill, an economy that has defied expectations, and a prescription drug bill that lowered the cost of insulin to $35 a month for seniors.
sentences.21: Biden also noted that Democrats passed the bipartisan Safer Communities Act—the first major gun safety bill in three decades. (Meanwhile, Biden said, his 'predecessor' told the NRA that he was 'proud he did nothing on guns when he was president.' After a school shooting in Iowa, Biden also accurately recounted that Trump told people to 'get over it.')
sentences.22: Biden additionally tried to move the needle on stubborn negative perceptions of the economy by championing economic indicators that are trending in a positive direction after the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.23: 'I inherited an economy that was on the brink,' he said. 'Now our economy is the envy of the world.'
sentences.24: Biden made a conscious effort to brag about the economy, a departure from previous joint addresses when Biden was tentative about his economic accomplishments. This time, he boasted about 15 million new jobs in three years, unemployment near 50-year lows, and steady wage growth.
sentences.25: But Biden also didn't shirk away from addressing inflation. He instead tried to empathize with Americans who still face the challenges of rising costs and presented it as a problem that Republicans were refusing to address.
sentences.26: 'Snack companies think you won't notice when they charge you just as much for the same size bag but with fewer chips in it,' Biden said with a laugh, imploring lawmakers to pass Sen. Bob Casey's (D-PA) bill to 'put a stop to shrinkflation.'
sentences.27: Biden seemed determined to make headlines for the political nature of his one hour and seven minute speech rather than giving a 'sleepy' address. While he slurred and stuttered over some words, he tried to match the deeply partisan spirit that Republicans brought to the chamber Thursday night while delivering a high-energy performance.
sentences.28: The strategy seemed to work. Republicans emerged from the House chamber offended and ready to criticize Biden for his partisan shots, but what they weren't doing was making the same jokes about his old age and confusion that kicked off the night.
sentences.29: Biden's frequent asides and clear willingness to banter with Republicans seemed to quell the most effective talking point against the president—that he's too senile to be president. Still, Biden also tried humor to neutralize that attack.
sentences.30: 'In my career, I've been told I was too young,' Biden said, noting that, when he first came to Washington, 'they didn't let me on the Senate elevators for votes sometimes—not a joke.'
sentences.31: But he also noted that he's been told, 'I'm too old.'
sentences.32: Biden said the issue facing our nation wasn't 'how old we are—it's how old our ideas are.'
sentences.33: 'Hate, anger, revenge, retribution are among the oldest of ideas,' he said. 'But you can't lead America with ancient ideas that only take us back.'
sentences.34: He said to lead America, you need a vision for the future, one where 'we defend democracy, not diminish it.'
sentences.35: 'I see a future for all Americans,' he said.

Explanation.explanation: Instead of focusing on policies or actions, Biden repeatedly attacks Trump's character and decisions, referring to him in a derogatory manner.
Biden redirects discussions about specific issues to criticize Trump's past actions, diverting from the current policies or proposals.
Biden uses emotionally charged anecdotes to criticize the opposition, invoking feelings rather than logical arguments.
Biden selectively highlights Democratic achievements without acknowledging any shortcomings, creating a biased perspective.
Biden draws broad conclusions about the economy based on selective positive indicators without considering the broader context.
Biden argues against old ideas by appealing to their age, suggesting they are inherently negative because they are not new.

cases.name: Biden slammed on social media after announcing Transgender Day of Visibility on Easter Sunday

sentences.1: President Joe Biden was slammed on social media Saturday after marking Easter Sunday, the most solemn Christian holiday, as 'Transgender Day of Visibility.'
