sentences.11: "This is a direct assault on Christianity. It's evident the left is determined to undermine our religion and traditions," she wrote on X. "This isn't just blatant disregard, it's intentional."
sentences.12: Conservative commentator Benny Johnson shared a screenshot of the White House statement, writing alongside it, "What a slap in the face to all Christians in Americaâ€¦"
sentences.13: Biden has previously come under fire for his stance on LGBTQ+ and abortion issues given his own position as a "devout Catholic" who regularly attends church.
sentences.14: The White House also used the same terminology when addressing Biden's pro-choice stance on abortion.
sentences.15: A recent poll from Pew Research found that just 13% of Americans think of Biden as "very religious," while 41% say he is "somewhat religious" and another 44% say he is "not at all" or "not too religious."

Explanation.explanation: The argument is suggesting that the timing of Transgender Day of Visibility on Easter Sunday is wrong because it disrupts a long-standing Christian tradition.
The argument concludes that the timing of the announcement is a direct attack on Christianity without sufficient evidence to support this claim.
This argument dismisses Biden's stance on LGBTQ+ and abortion issues based on his religious practices instead of addressing the policies themselves.
The argument appeals to the emotions of Christians by describing the announcement as a 'slap in the face,' which aims to provoke an emotional reaction rather than addressing the policy.

cases.name: Georgia election charges should be tossed, acts are protected by 1st amendment: Trump attorney

sentences.1: In a hearing Thursday in Fulton County Superior Court, lawyers for former President Trump and co-defendants argued that the sweeping election interference case against him should be tossed, citing First Amendment protections for political speech.
sentences.2: Judge Scott McAfee presided over the hearing Thursday morning in the first court appearance in the Trump case since ordering District Attorney Fani Willis to remove special counsel Nathan Wade from the case over their romantic affair.
sentences.3: McAfee heard arguments related to motions from Trump and co-defendant David Shafer, the former chairman of the Georgia Republican Party, who his lawyer says acted legally when he and other state Republicans signed a certificate asserting that Trump won the 2020 presidential election in Georgia.
sentences.4: Steve Sadow, counsel for the former president and presumptive GOP nominee in the 2024 election, argued Thursday, 'There is nothing alleged against President Trump that is not political speech.'
sentences.5: Sadow quoted from a dissent in a key Supreme Court case, United States v. Alvarez, written by Justices Clarence Thomas, Samuel Alito and the late Justice Antonin Scalia, which says 'even where there is a wide scholarly consensus concerning a particular matter, the truth is served by allowing that consensus to be challenged without fear of reprisal.'
sentences.6: 'Today's accepted wisdom sometimes turns out to be mistaken. And in these contexts, even a false statement may be deemed to make a valuable contribution to public debate, since it brings about the clear perception and livelier impression of truth produced by its collusion with error,' Sadow read from the dissent.
sentences.7: 'That's the essence of what we have right here. That's the facts that have been alleged,' Sadow said.
sentences.8: 'Essentially, the state's position is, because - as alleged - what President Trump said speech-wise or expressed either through his speech or conduct, which is still freedom of expression, because that's false in the eyes of the state, it's lost all protection to the First Amendment.' Sadow argued, adding that Supreme Court justices concluded 'just the opposite' in their dissent.
sentences.9: A lawyer for the state pushed back, saying 'what we have heard here today is an attempt to rewrite the indictment, to take out the parts that are inconvenient and only say, 'Well, it's all speech, it's all talking.''
sentences.10: 'He was just the guy asking questions and not someone who was part of an overarching criminal conspiracy, trying to overturn election results for an election he did not win by violating the RICO statute, by making false statements to the government, by filing false documents, by impersonating officers, and doing a whole host of other activity which is harmful in addition to the falsity of the statements employed to make them happen,' the state's lawyer added.
sentences.11: Trump was indicted in August on charges that include the Georgia RICO Act - the Racketeer Influenced And Corrupt Organizations Act; solicitation of violation of oath by a public officer; conspiracy to commit impersonating a public officer; conspiracy to commit forgery in the first degree; conspiracy to commit false statements and writings; conspiracy to commit filing false documents; conspiracy to commit forgery in the first degree; and filing false documents.
sentences.12: In March, Judge McAfee tossed six of the charges against Trump and his co-defendants, saying the state failed to allege sufficient detail for six counts of 'solicitation of violation of oath by public officer.'

Explanation.explanation: The mention of District Attorney Fani Willis's romantic affair with special counsel Nathan Wade is irrelevant to the main issue of the hearing.

Sadow's use of a dissent from a Supreme Court case to support his argument relies on the authority of the justices, but the dissent does not have the weight of a majority opinion and may not be directly applicable to the case at hand.
Sadow's assertion that 'There is nothing alleged against President Trump that is not political speech' is a broad conclusion that does not consider the specifics of the allegations.

cases.name: California votes to spend $6.4B on homeless crisis despite spiraling debt

sentences.1: A ballot measure that would require California to spend billions of dollars on the state's spiraling homeless crisis was passed by a razor-thin majority Wednesday, two weeks after residents cast their votes.
sentences.2: Proposition 1 requires strict requirements on counties to spend on housing and drug treatment programs for homeless people, as well as allowing the state to raise a $6.4 billion bond to tackle the issue.
sentences.3: The measure comes as the Golden State's budget debt is expected to grow to $73 billion this year, according to Bloomberg.
sentences.4: A signature proposal by Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, the measure was approved by 50.2% of nearly 7.2 million voters, a slim majority unforeseen just a few months ago.
sentences.5: "This is the biggest change in decades in how California tackles homelessness and a victory for doing things radically different," Newsom said in a statement after the borderline vote.
sentences.6: "Now, counties and local officials must match the ambition of California voters.
sentences.7: This historic reform will only succeed if we all kick into action immediately - state government and local leaders, together."
sentences.8: The state will now be able to borrow $6.38 billion to build 4,350 housing units, half of which will be reserved for veterans, and add 6,800 mental health and addiction treatment beds.
sentences.9: Counties will also be required to spend about two-thirds of funds raised from a 2004-enacted wealth tax on mental health services on housing and programs for homeless people with serious mental illnesses or substance abuse problems.
sentences.10: The state needs some 8,000 more beds to treat mental health and addiction issues.
sentences.11: Between $2 billion and $3 billion a year is raised from the tax, and it provides about one-third of the state's total mental health budget.
sentences.12: Newsom's administration has already spent at least $22 billion on various programs to address the crisis over the last few years, including $3.5 billion to convert rundown motels into homeless housing.
sentences.13: At the same time, its homeless population has ballooned to around 181,000.
sentences.14: The measure looked sure to pass when introduced by Newsom and a group of bipartisan legislators last year.
sentences.15: Democrats outnumber Republicans by about 2 to 1 in the state.
sentences.16: However, it snuck through by a paper-thin majority.
sentences.17: Proposition 1 collected more than $15.7 million, with a donor list that included a Bay Area tribe, labor unions, builders, health care providers, Uber and the California Chamber of Commerce, The New York Times reported.
sentences.18: The only organized opposition collected a mere $1,000.
sentences.19: Opponents, including social service providers and county officials, said the change will threaten programs that are not solely focused on housing or drug treatment but keep people from becoming homeless in the first place.
sentences.20: Critics have also said that rural counties with far fewer homeless people per capita will be forced to divert a larger percentage of funds to housing.

Explanation.explanation: Newsom's statement that this measure is the biggest change in decades and a victory for doing things radically different is a questionable conclusion without clear evidence backing it.
The statement that this reform will only succeed if everyone takes immediate action is a questionable conclusion as it assumes collective action is the only path to success.
The need for 8,000 more beds to treat mental health and addiction issues is stated as a fact without current context or comparison, appealing to a traditional view that more beds are always needed.

Newsom's administration spending at least $22 billion on various programs is presented as a long-term ongoing effort without addressing its effectiveness, appealing to the tradition of continuous spending.
Stating that Democrats outnumber Republicans by about 2 to 1 as a reason for the measure passing is an appeal to the traditional political landscape without examining the measure itself.

cases.name: Alabama governor signs bill protecting IVF into law: 'Proud we are a pro-life, pro-family state'

sentences.1: Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey signed a bill into law Wednesday evening protecting in vitro fertilization (IVF) treatments after a February decision by the state Supreme Court led some fertility clinics to pause their procedures.
sentences.2: Senate Bill 159, a bipartisan piece of legislation, was met with heavy support from state lawmakers and quickly moved through the legislature to ensure clinics could confidently resume operations for IVF patients.
sentences.3: "Alabama works to foster a culture of life, and that certainly includes IVF," Ivey said in a statement Wednesday night.
sentences.4: "I am pleased to sign this important, short-term measure into law so that couples in Alabama hoping and praying to be parents can grow their families through IVF."
sentences.5: The law is designed to protect medical professionals from civil and criminal immunity in case of unintentional death or damage to an embryo following a ruling made by the state Supreme Court allowing three couples who lost frozen embryos during a mishap at a storage facility to file for wrongful death claims.
sentences.6: The Justices cited language in the Alabama Constitution that allows parents to sue over the death of a minor child and said that the 1872 law "applies to all unborn children, regardless of their location."
sentences.7: Alabamians also voted in 2018 to add language recognizing the "rights of unborn children."
sentences.8: "Unborn children are 'children' ... without exception based on developmental stage, physical location, or any other ancillary characteristics," Justice Jay Mitchell wrote in the ruling.
sentences.9: Justice Greg Cook, who filed the only full dissent to the majority opinion, said a minor is not defined under the state's Wrongful Death of a Minor Act and that using the law to cover frozen embryos is stretching original intent.
sentences.10: Ivey said she understands IVF is a "complex issue" and she anticipates "there will be more work to come," but the priority was to "provide the assurances" fertility clinics needed so the ones who paused treatments could "resume services immediately."
sentences.11: "Let me say clearly: Alabama supports growing families through IVF.
sentences.12: From protecting the unborn to supporting IVF, Alabama is proud we are a pro-life, pro-family state," Ivey said.
sentences.13: Alabama Fertility, one of the clinics that paused IVF treatments last month, said on its Instagram page Wednesday afternoon before the bill became law that it is "ready to re-start IVF treatments as soon as tomorrow."
sentences.14: The law is effective immediately and applies retroactively, excluding pending litigation.

Explanation.explanation: The argument refers to the Alabama Constitution and a 2018 vote to justify the law, implying that because these traditions exist, the law is justified without addressing current ethical or scientific debates.
Ivey’s statement that Alabama is proud to be a pro-life, pro-family state relies on the tradition of these values to support the law without engaging with contemporary counterarguments.

The statement that Alabama works to foster a culture of life and that includes IVF is a questionable conclusion because it assumes that supporting IVF is inherently part of fostering a culture of life without providing evidence or reasoning for this connection.

The statement that Alabama is proud to be a pro-life, pro-family state as a justification for the law is a questionable conclusion because it assumes that these values inherently support the law without addressing potential conflicts or nuances.

cases.name: Mayorkas impeachment trial poised to pressure these vulnerable Senate Dems

sentences.1: Democrats up for re-election in battleground states face a bind in the Senate as the impeachment trial for Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas is expected to begin this month over his role in the ongoing crisis at the southern border.
sentences.2: Several Republican Senate sources told Fox News Digital they expect the pressure to ramp up for lawmakers such as Sens. Jon Tester, D-Mont., Jacky Rosen, D-Nev., Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., Sherrod Brown, D-Ohio, and Bob Casey, D-Penn., who face competitive re-election races in November.
sentences.3: Voters in each of the senators' states have indicated strong concerns over the state of the border.
sentences.4: Republican senators recently accused Tester of being unwilling to vote on border or immigration-related amendments during negotiations over the $1.2 trillion spending package that caused a brief partial government shutdown before being passed last month.
sentences.5: Tester's office denied the claims.
sentences.6: One senior Republican Senate source predicted Tester would be similarly pushed during the impeachment trial procedure: "He'll have to go on the record with it. No way out," the source said.
sentences.7: They noted that Brown would also be put to the test in the Mayorkas trial.
sentences.8: A representative for Tester told Fox News Digital on Wednesday, "Senator Tester will review the articles when they are sent over to the Senate."
sentences.9: The House passed two articles of impeachment against Mayorkas in early February but held onto them until after the appropriations process finished.
sentences.10: In a letter last week, House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., revealed his intention to deliver the articles to the Senate on April 10 and urged Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., to move quickly on a trial.
sentences.11: When the articles are delivered, "all senators have to be sworn in as jurors and sign the book," a senior GOP source said.
sentences.12: "We actually go into trial mode, but Schumer will put forward a vote to dismiss it," the source predicted.
sentences.13: Schumer's office did not provide comment to Fox News Digital.
sentences.14: "Everything is simple majority," the source noted, meaning only 51 of the 100 senators are necessary to move forward with any action.
sentences.15: While Senate Democrats have largely dismissed the charges against Mayorkas as meritless and political posturing, the lawmakers who are competing in close races in the general election may be influenced by the growing concern over the border among their constituents.
sentences.16: In a March Fox News Poll, 41% of all registered voters agreed the situation at the southern border is an emergency.
sentences.17: This included 65% of Republicans, 31% of independents and 20% of Democrats.
sentences.18: As a result, the vulnerable Democrat senators are certain to be met with attacks on the campaign trail from their Republican opponents, who will pose the question of their seriousness on the border crisis.
sentences.19: In a February memo from National Republican Senatorial Committee political director Tim Edson that was obtained by Fox News Digital, Senate candidates were advised to hold their Democrat counterparts accountable.
sentences.20: "We cannot allow Senate Democrats to sweep the Biden Administration's failures at the southern border under the rug," it reads.
sentences.21: "Democrats caused this crisis, and voting to acquit Mayorkas is a vote to allow the continued invasion of our country."
sentences.22: Tester's opponent, Republican Senate candidate Tim Sheehy, said in a statement that "the Senate should hold a full impeachment trial."
sentences.23: "Senator Jon Tester wants to avoid a trial and let Mayorkas off the hook because they BOTH support the radical Left's push of open borders and letting illegal immigrants flood into America.
sentences.24: We deserve accountability!" he continued.
sentences.25: Representatives for Rosen, Baldwin, Brown and Casey did not provide comment to Fox News Digital.
sentences.26: "If Bob Casey is serious about securing the border, he'll urge Chuck Schumer to move this inquiry forward and hold them accountable," said Pennsylvania Republican Senate front-runner Dave McCormick in a statement to Fox News Digital.
sentences.27: Spokesperson Ben Voelkel for Wisconsin Republican Senate front-runner Eric Hovde said in a statement, "Sen. Baldwin needs to hold [Mayorkas] accountable.
sentences.28: If she doesn't, Wisconsin voters will hold her accountable for her inaction."
sentences.29: "If Sherrod Brown cares about hardworking Ohioans who have been impacted by the border invasion and fentanyl crisis, he will hold Mayorkas accountable in the Senate trial," said Reagan McCarthy, spokesperson for Ohio Republican Senate candidate Bernie Moreno.
sentences.30: Sen. Joe Manchin, D-W.Va., who has occasionally been out of step with Democrats, appears likely to stick with his caucus in the likely case they look to dismiss the trial quickly.
sentences.31: In February, he told Politico that the forthcoming impeachment was "Pure crap," adding that he wants "No trial at all."
sentences.32: Manchin's office referred Fox News Digital to his previous comment.
sentences.33: Republican strategist Brian Walsh, a former staffer for Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, said, "It highlights a huge political vulnerability for Democratic Senators like Jon Tester, Sherrod Brown and Bob Casey going into the 2024 election."
sentences.34: They will be forced to "pick a side" between their base and "the majority of voters, including independents" who say the border is the most important problem in the country, Walsh added.
sentences.35: As the senators face a difficult decision, it's not clear that all Republicans will be on board to continue the trial.
sentences.36: Each vote matters, given the Senate's narrow 49-51 split between Republicans and those in the Democrat caucus.
sentences.37: Sen. Mitt Romney, R-Utah, criticized the idea of a trial in late February, writing on X, formerly known as Twitter, that it "might be great politics, but it's not the remedy for bad policy & would set a terrible constitutional precedent."
sentences.38: Romney's office did not provide comment to Fox News Digital.
sentences.39: Other concerns for the impeachment effort are Sens. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, and Susan Collins, R-Maine, who have gone against the conference previously.
sentences.40: Neither of their offices provided comment to Fox News Digital on the subject.
sentences.41: Meanwhile, Mayorkas is set to appear on Capitol Hill on April 10, the same day the articles of impeachment are expected to be delivered to the Senate, for an unrelated hearing before the House Appropriations Homeland Security Subcommittee regarding the department's fiscal 2025 request.

Explanation.explanation: The speaker uses emotional language such as 'radical Left's push of open borders' and 'illegal immigrants flood into America' to appeal to fear and anger.
The speaker appeals to emotions by mentioning the fentanyl crisis to gain support for holding Mayorkas accountable.
The speaker appeals to tradition by suggesting that failing to hold the Biden Administration accountable is sweeping the issue 'under the rug.'
The speaker appeals to tradition by framing the situation as an 'invasion of our country,' implying a historical or traditional view of borders.
The statement forces a choice between the senators' base and 'the majority of voters,' ignoring any middle ground or nuanced positions they might take.
The conclusion that voting to acquit Mayorkas is a vote to allow the 'continued invasion of our country' is not necessarily warranted by the evidence provided.
The statement that allowing Mayorkas off the hook implies supporting open borders is a questionable conclusion without further evidence.
The statement by Romney shifts the discussion from the impeachment trial's purpose to its political and constitutional implications, sidetracking from the main issue.

cases.name: Why Teck Resources' proposed split never made much sense and shareholders shot it down

sentences.1: It took Teck Resources Ltd. TECK-B-T 2½ years to structure the spinout of its steelmaking coal business, and only a few hours for the idea to be shot down by outsiders.
sentences.2: When Teck announced its split in February, the Canadian miner seemed, at first, to be giving shareholders concerned about environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles the divestment of its coal division that they'd long dreamed of.
sentences.3: Chief executive Jonathan Price used grandiose words, pitching it as the creation of 'two great, sustainable companies, set up for success.'
sentences.4: Yet once the news was digested, a central piece of the proposal stood out: Although Teck would be split into two companies - its existing metals business and a new publicly traded company, Elk Valley Resources Ltd., that held the coal assets - almost all the money from both would flow to one because 90 per cent of Elk Valley's cash flows would be sent back to Teck for an estimated 11 years.
sentences.5: The day the deal was announced, Royal Bank of Canada analyst Sam Crittenden summarized the proposal rather succinctly: 'In the near term, the new Teck seems similar to the old Teck.'
sentences.6: On Wednesday, shareholders confirmed they felt the same way, with enough voting against the split to force Teck to scrap the proposal and go back to the drawing board.
sentences.7: As Mr. Price explained on a conference call, shareholders are all for the coal divestment, just not the one Teck took years to craft with the expensive assistance of seven investment banks.
sentences.8: 'They would like to see a simpler and more direct separation,' he explained.
sentences.9: To Teck's credit, management had good intentions.
sentences.10: Before the pandemic, the share prices of so many resource companies were in the dumps because investors were more ESG conscious.
sentences.11: At the start of 2020, Teck's shares were trading around $20 a share, roughly one-third of their current price.
sentences.12: To adapt, Teck's board of directors held 'strategic discussions' with the miner's management team in 2019, according to regulatory filings, and some of the ideas thrown around included selling or spinning off Teck's energy business - it had a 21-per-cent stake in the Fort Hills oil sands project - as well as its entire coal division.
sentences.13: But Teck was in a pickle.
sentences.14: Even though its steelmaking coal business is less carbon intensive than mining thermal coal, which is used for power generation, its coal wasn't exactly clean, and that narrowed the roster of prospective buyers.
sentences.15: Teck also couldn't afford to simply spin the division out and give investors the choice to hold or sell the new coal company shares, because it needed the coal cash flow to fund the expansion of a major copper project in northern Chile, Quebrada Blanca Phase 2, or QB2.
sentences.16: In late 2019 and early 2020, Ardea Partners LLP, an independent advisory firm run by former Goldman Sachs bankers, presented all the strategic alternatives available to Teck, including a full-blown sale of the coal division.
sentences.17: Management was asked to evaluate the options, and by early 2022, it went back to the board with some pretty firm beliefs.
sentences.18: Executives had reviewed all the options, and they shot down most of them, including: selling the coal business to another steelmaking coal operator or private equity firm; a strategic joint venture; a merger with an existing coal company; and a complete spin-off with no access to coal's cash flows.
sentences.19: It wasn't that some of these options couldn't be pulled off.
sentences.20: In fact, at one point there were two offers to sell off large stakes in the coal business, which could have provided some upfront cash that supplanted 10 years of cash flows, according to filings.
sentences.21: However, Teck said in a filing that 'neither expression of interest was viewed as attractive at that time due to the valuation assumptions underlying such offers.'
sentences.22: Management also said it shot down the other options because of concerns about 'viability, value, execution risk and failure to meet Teck's strategic goals,' according to filings.
sentences.23: The only option, then, was to proceed with the convoluted spinout, and ultimately the board got behind the idea, arguing that it would provide investors with 'a choice of allocating investments to one or both of two businesses with very different commodity fundamentals and value propositions.'
sentences.24: The only problem: It wasn't true.
sentences.25: This wasn't really a spinout.
sentences.26: It was more like shuffling deck chairs, and shareholders saw through it.
sentences.27: And now any potential partner, or buyer, of the coal business knows it has the upper hand in any negotiation.

Explanation.explanation: Using emotive language like 'grandiose words' and 'simpler and more direct separation' to appeal to shareholders' emotions.
Concluding that the spinout wasn't true and was just 'shuffling deck chairs' without providing sufficient evidence.
Introducing unrelated points like the impact of ESG consciousness on share prices and the cleanliness of coal to sidetrack from the main issue of the spinout structure.

cases.name: Seven stats to amaze and depress all who own a house or hope to own

sentences.1: Housing is hot - again. Across the country, in cities big and small, prices are surging after a summer lull.
sentences.2: Here are some numbers that document what's happening:
sentences.3: $1-million
sentences.4: Toronto and Vancouver could soon have company in the club of cities with average resale home prices of $1-million or more.
sentences.5: Hamilton, a steel industry town just to the west of Toronto, is on the verge along with nearby Burlington.
sentences.6: The average resale price for these cities in October was $946,300, up 29.4 per cent from $731,500 in the same month last year.
sentences.7: Other prospects for the million-dollar club include the Southern Ontario communities of Cambridge and Guelph, both with average prices in the $825,000 range; and Victoria, where the average resale price last month was $871,000.
sentences.8: 18.8 per cent
sentences.9: That's the year-over-year increase in home prices in the Yukon, where the entire population wouldn't fill the stadium where the Toronto Blue Jays play, at least in non-pandemic conditions.
sentences.10: The average price Yukon price was $542,515 last month, up almost $86,000 from $456,771 in the same month in 2020.
sentences.11: Could this be British Columbia's rising price trend spreading north?
sentences.12: Provincially, the average price increase in B.C. last month was also 18.8 per cent.
sentences.14: In Barrie, roughly an hour's drive north of Toronto in rarely seen clear traffic, the average house price in the past year jumped to $786,500 from $579,400, a difference of $207,100.
sentences.15: That last amount of money would very nearly buy you a typical house in Moose Jaw.
sentences.16: Some numbers on the commute to Toronto from Barrie on GO Transit - 90 minutes each way by train, with a round trip costing around $25 if you buy a Presto fare card instead of paying cash.
sentences.17: Six things a brutally honest banker would tell you about mortgages, HELOCs and market-linked GICs
sentences.18: 1.503 per cent
sentences.19: The yield on the five-year Government of Canada bond hit this mark late at midday Wednesday, which was up from 0.39 per cent at the beginning of the year and a hair's distance from where it stood before the pandemic.
sentences.20: Why you should care: Five-year government bond yields set the trend for fixed mortgage rates.
sentences.21: The Ratehub.ca historical mortgage rate database says discounted five-year fixed mortgage rates were as low as 1.39 per cent at the beginning of the year, which compares with current rates in the 2.35-per-cent to 2.59-per-cent range at national mortgage brokerage companies.
sentences.22: Buyers are keeping purchases affordable with variable-rate mortgages, which can be had at rates that are one percentage point and more below fixed five-year rates.
sentences.23: With a variable-rate mortgage, you're subject to every increase coming in the Bank of Canada overnight rate in the next 12 to 18 months.
sentences.24: Four
sentences.25: The federal Liberals made many promises during the recent election campaign to improve housing affordability, including measures to promote construction of affordable housing, curb flipping and discourage buying by foreign investors.
sentences.26: At least four additional promises will make it easier to afford the purchase of a house, which is to say they will stimulate demand and prices.
sentences.27: A standout affordability promise is to make mortgage default insurance available for homes valued at $1.25-million, up from the current $1-million, and then index this price to inflation.
sentences.28: As a result, buyers in Toronto and Vancouver will be able to put a minimum of 5 per cent down on a home instead of the current 20 per cent minimum applying to homes valued at $1-million or more.
sentences.29: 30 per cent
sentences.30: That's the ballpark level of year-over-year price growth in both New Brunswick and Ontario.
sentences.31: An odd partnership has emerged between these two provinces.
sentences.32: Ontario's rising prices are driving residents out of the province to places such as Saint John and Moncton, both of which reported price gains last month of more than 27 per cent.
sentences.33: The New Brunswick benchmark price in October was $267,000, compared with an average price of $912,763 in Ontario.
sentences.34: Nationally, resale house prices jumped 18.2 to $716,585.
sentences.35: 2.5 per cent
sentences.36: An HR consulting firm called LifeWorks has reported that employers are projecting average annual pay increases next year of around 2.5 per cent.
sentences.37: The gap between income and house prices keeps widening.

Explanation.explanation: The statement 'Could this be British Columbia's rising price trend spreading north?' is a questionable conclusion because it assumes a direct cause without sufficient evidence.

The assertion that four promises will 'make it easier to afford the purchase of a house, which is to say they will stimulate demand and prices' assumes a direct cause-effect relationship without presenting evidence.

The conclusion that the year-over-year price growth in New Brunswick and Ontario is indicative of an odd partnership between these provinces is a hasty generalization, drawing a broad conclusion from limited data.

The statement that buyers in Toronto and Vancouver will be able to put a minimum of 5 per cent down on a home instead of 20 per cent because of a change in mortgage default insurance is an appeal to tradition, implying that the traditional way of putting a lower down payment should be maintained.

cases.name: Flood-damaged Vancouver, southern B.C. railways expected to remain impassable for days

sentences.1: The railways that link Vancouver and the southern part of British Columbia with the rest of the country are expected to remain flood-damaged and impassable for days.
sentences.2: Rail lines owned by Canadian National Railway Co. and Canadian Pacific Railway Ltd. run along the Fraser River, which spilled its banks and cut off roads, bridges and tracks in this week's heavy rain and flooding.
sentences.3: Mathieu Gaudreault, a CN spokesperson, said crews are making progress on repairing the railway, but he declined to estimate when the tracks would open.
sentences.4: "Traffic through southern B.C., northbound and eastbound traffic from Vancouver, as well as inbound traffic to Vancouver from east/north of Kamloops are still affected by the situation," Mr. Gaudreault said.
sentences.5: CP's tracks between Spence's Bridge and Falls Creek are blocked as a result of flood damage in several sections, said Salem Woodrow, a CP spokesperson.
sentences.6: The washouts have halted freight on CP's busiest rail corridor, which links Vancouver's port with shippers of grain, consumer goods and other products.
sentences.7: "There is no time estimate for when service will resume," Ms. Woodrow said.
sentences.8: B.C. declared a state of emergency on Wednesday after the record rainfall damaged thousands of homes and cut off supply lines.
sentences.9: At least one person has died.
sentences.10: Some roadways have reopened as the water recedes, but the damage to key transport routes will take days to repair.
sentences.11: "CP has deployed crews and equipment to the region, and CP engineering teams are working to repair the damaged rail corridor as quickly as possible where safe to do so," Ms. Woodrow said.
sentences.12: Work to repair the washed-out tracks is being slowed by three sinkholes that have formed beneath CN's railway.
sentences.13: Walter Spracklin, a Royal Bank of Canada stock analyst, said CN executives told him the railway will not be repaired before this weekend and could be out until next week.
sentences.14: In a note to clients, Mr. Spracklin said the loss of key routes will reduce cargo volumes and drive up costs and capital expenses for both railways, but will have little - if any - impact on the companies' share prices.
sentences.15: CP and CN's share prices are down by 3 per cent and less than 1 per cent, respectively, this week.
sentences.16: Climate Scientist and Professor Simon Donner explains what the phenomenon 'atmospheric river' is and why the one that hit Western Canada dumped record breaking amounts of rain in the Lower Mainland of British Columbia.

Explanation.explanation: Walter Spracklin, a stock analyst, is quoted making a prediction about the railway repair timeline based on what CN executives told him. This is an appeal to authority because Spracklin may not have the expertise to assess the accuracy of the repair timeline himself.

The statement that the loss of key routes will reduce cargo volumes and drive up costs but will have little impact on share prices is a questionable conclusion. It assumes a direct and simplistic relationship between operational disruptions and share prices without considering other market factors.

cases.name: Canada's largest school board doesn't seem to understand the indispensable role of defence lawyers in our justice system

sentences.1: Canada's largest school board doesn't seem to understand the indispensable role of defence lawyers in our justice system
sentences.2: Carissima Mathen, LSM, is professor of law at the University of Ottawa. Her books include Courts Without Cases: The Law and Politics of Advisory Opinions.
sentences.3: "Does it ever bother you, defending people you know are guilty?"
sentences.4: That's one of the most common questions defence lawyers get from people who are unfamiliar with the job.
sentences.5: The legendary Canadian lawyer Edward Greenspan had perhaps the best answer: "If I defended crimes, maybe it would - but I don't defend crimes. I only defend innocent people. Until they are found guilty, there are no other kinds of people for me to defend."
sentences.6: I was reminded of Mr. Greenspan's words in light of a controversy involving the Toronto District School Board and Marie Henein, one of Canada's best known criminal lawyers who represented former CBC Radio host Jian Ghomeshi.
sentences.7: Her memoir, Nothing But The Truth, was proposed for a book club series to which the TDSB sometimes sends students.
sentences.8: The club's organizer says that a superintendent told her that the book was not suitable because Ms. Henein "defended Jian Ghomeshi and how do you explain that to little girls." (The board now says it is reviewing the book and developing a broader policy for future events.)
sentences.9: There are many legitimate reasons why a particular book might not suit a particular reading group.
sentences.10: The TDSB's rejection, however, was because the author had defended - and successfully, at that - a high-profile person against charges of sexual assault.
sentences.11: After #MeToo, the TDSB superintended signalled, her book should apparently be avoided.
sentences.12: This messaging - to students and to the public at large - is deeply problematic, for at least two reasons.
sentences.13: First, being a defence lawyer is a difficult, occasionally vexing role - and yet it is extraordinarily important.
sentences.14: The whole point is to disrupt what might otherwise be a frogmarch to conviction.
sentences.15: The more heinous the alleged crime, and the more the Crown's accusations stoke fear and revulsion, the more zealous a defence lawyer is called to be - and, indeed, needs to be.
sentences.16: There are few principles in our legal system as important as this one to ensure that we remain governed by the law, and not driven by the mob.
sentences.17: And make no mistake: Public opinion makes a real difference to the working conditions of criminal defence lawyers.
sentences.18: The public often is outraged at criminal cases - not just at accused persons, but everyone involved in their trials - and defence lawyers are easy fodder when an acquittal is viewed as unjust, as some clearly see Mr. Ghomeshi's 2016 judgment.
sentences.19: However, the great majority of criminal lawyers never achieve Ms. Henein's prominence.
sentences.20: They often have to rely on Legal Aid, which is always an easy target for politicians looking to reduce or redistribute budgetary expenses.
sentences.21: Denigrating the role of defence lawyers, as the TDSB did, makes it easier to justify cuts to Legal Aid that will have very real downstream effects on indigent and marginalized defendants.
sentences.22: Second, the TDSB's actions send a terrible message to women and girls considering a career in law.
sentences.23: Sexual assault is a gendered crime, and the historically male-dominated defence bar has sometimes contributed to difficulties ensuring fairness to all parties.
sentences.24: It makes sense to encourage women and girls to enter the field.
sentences.25: Yet some people are clearly disturbed that Ms. Henein could have possibly achieved such success by, in part, representing men charged with sexual offences.
sentences.26: "How can she defend him?" has become the sequel of defence lawyers' most commonly faced question.
sentences.27: It subjects women to different professional expectations, while also continuing a worrying societal trend in which personal identity and professional obligations are merged.
sentences.28: No one is required to admire Ms. Henein, buy her book or accept her arguments.
sentences.29: Individuals should feel free to dislike the techniques she employed in defending her client at trial.
sentences.30: But public institutions, such as the TDSB, are not individuals.
sentences.31: As an educational organization, it has a higher responsibility to ensure that it is not contributing to ill-informed opinions about the criminal justice system and the actors who make it function, and passing those on to our youth.
sentences.32: None of this means that defence lawyers should be immune from criticism.
sentences.33: Their conduct is subject to legal and professional standards which, if violated, triggers appeals or disciplinary proceedings.
sentences.34: But nothing in Ms. Henein's conduct came close to crossing those lines.
sentences.35: She was a fearsome advocate for Mr. Ghomeshi, employing the available rules to devastating effect - as the system allowed, and as her role required.
sentences.36: I have defended reforms to sexual-assault law for more than 20 years.
sentences.37: I know well the uncompromising, even brutal nature of our far-from-perfect system, and that it should be subject to continual review and scrutiny.
sentences.38: But, as Ms. Henein herself has said, it is the system we have.
sentences.39: And in its basic precepts - the presumption of innocence, the heavy burden on the Crown - it outshines pretty much any alternative.

Explanation.explanation: The discussion shifts from the book club's decision to the general working conditions and public perception of defence lawyers.
The argument sidetracks to the funding of Legal Aid, which is not directly relevant to the book's suitability for the reading group.
The argument appeals to emotions by discussing the impact on women and girls considering a career in law, rather than addressing the specific issue of the book's content and suitability.
The question 'How can she defend him?' appeals to the emotional reaction of defending those charged with serious crimes, which clouds the objective evaluation of the book's content.
The argument appeals to tradition by suggesting that the current system, despite its flaws, is better than any alternative, without providing evidence for why this tradition should be maintained.

cases.name: Rogers CEO Joe Natale's demands rejected by board, leading to his exit

sentences.1: Joe Natale presented the board of Rogers Communications Inc. RCI-B-Twith a list of demands aimed at protecting his authority as CEO, but the board rejected the requests, resulting in his dismissal this week.
sentences.2: The board of the telecom and media giant voted on Tuesday night to remove Mr. Natale as chief executive officer and install Tony Staffieri, the company's former chief financial officer, in the role on an interim basis.
sentences.3: The move followed weeks of boardroom tension that broke out in late September, when chair Edward Rogers attempted to put Mr. Staffieri into the top job.
sentences.4: Before Tuesday's meeting, the board was presented with a document outlining Mr. Natale's requests, according to five sources familiar with the matter.
sentences.5: The Rogers family feud: From a butt-dial to a B.C. Supreme Court case, here's what's happening inside Canada's biggest telecom boardroom
sentences.6: Rogers removes CEO Joe Natale after boardroom power struggle for control of telecom giant
sentences.7: Rogers CEO Joe Natale learned of Edward Rogers's plan to oust him through butt-dial from CFO
sentences.8: The document indicated that Mr. Natale would remain at the helm of Canada's largest wireless carrier at least until the closing of the $26-billion acquisition of Shaw Communications Inc., according to the sources.
sentences.9: But it also stipulated that Mr. Natale would need discretion over hiring and firing members of his management team, some of the sources said.
sentences.10: The Globe and Mail is not identifying the sources because they are not authorized to speak publicly about the matter.
sentences.11: The document also specified that Mr. Staffieri not rejoin the company.
sentences.12: The chief financial officer left in late September after Mr. Natale overheard him discussing a plan that would give the top job to Mr. Staffieri and oust a number of senior executives.
sentences.13: It also asked that Robert DÃ©patie, a director who was to become president of the cable division under Mr. Rogers's plan, not join the management team, two of the sources said.
sentences.14: Mr. Natale's request regarding Mr. Staffieri was at odds with Mr. Rogers's desire to bring him back into the CFO role, several of the sources said.
sentences.15: Some board members felt that Mr. Staffieri's financial experience would help the company manage the debt it will need to take on to finance the Shaw takeover, according to one of the sources.
sentences.16: Mr. Natale attended the Tuesday evening meeting of the board, which Mr. Rogers recently reconstituted through a written resolution.
sentences.17: Several board members expressed outrage over some of the requests in the document, one source said.
sentences.18: Mr. Rogers, who is also chair of the family trust that controls the Toronto-based telecom, indicated that several conditions would interfere with the board's ability to oversee management, another said.
sentences.19: Among the key sticking points was a condition that directors would not engage directly with the company's employees other than members of the senior leadership team without the approval of the CEO or an executive.

sentences.22: Mr. Natale had also requested a two-person committee to mediate between himself and Mr. Rogers in case of a disagreement.

sentences.24: However, the majority of the board voted in favour of a resolution to remove Mr. Natale.

sentences.26: A spokesperson for Rogers Communications declined to comment.
sentences.27: The future of the Toronto-based telecom's senior leadership team is unclear.
sentences.28: Dave Fuller, the president of the company's wireless division, suggested in a court document that he would leave Rogers if Mr. Natale were no longer CEO.
sentences.29: Mr. Natale's dismissal was the latest event in a months-long battle for control of Rogers Communications.
sentences.30: The showdown broke out when Mr. Rogers's attempt to unseat Mr. Natale met resistance from the majority of the company's board, including his mother and sisters, and resulted in Mr. Staffieri leaving instead.
sentences.31: The board later voted to remove Mr. Rogers as chair, although an attempt by family members to restrain his ability to exercise his voting control over the company failed to garner sufficient support.
sentences.32: Mr. Rogers then announced plans to remove five of the company's independent directors and replace them with his own candidates.
sentences.33: The company challenged the legality of reconstituting the board in this manner, and for about two weeks, Rogers Communications essentially had two boards, each claiming to be the legitimate one.
sentences.34: On Nov. 5, a B.C. Supreme Court judge ruled that Mr. Rogers's move to replace the directors through a shareholder resolution is valid.
sentences.35: Robert Gemmell, the company's lead director, said in a statement on Tuesday evening that the board worked 'earnestly and in good faith' with Mr. Natale to establish a 'constructive working relationship' that would keep him on as CEO through the closing of the takeover.
sentences.36: However, an agreement could not be reached.
sentences.37: On Twitter, Martha Rogers noted on Tuesday evening that less than two weeks ago, on Nov. 5, Mr. Rogers had said that the board supports Mr. Natale as CEO.

cases.name: Trudeau wins no concessions on Buy America from Biden

sentences.1: U.S. President Joe Biden was unwilling to offer concessions to Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador of Mexico on proposed Buy American provisions, including tax incentives for U.S.-made electric vehicles that could cause future production of the vehicles to move away from Canada.

sentences.3: Despite Canada's warnings that the proposed incentives for U.S.-made electric vehicles would violate the United States-Mexico-Canada free trade agreement, Mr. Biden was non-committal about whether his administration would acquiesce to Mr. Trudeau's requests that America allow the tax credits to apply to Canadian-made vehicles too.
sentences.4: The credits are a component of Mr. Biden's U.S.$1.75-trillion Build Back Better program, which has yet to receive congressional approval.
sentences.5: Mr. Biden told reporters that he would not start negotiating a deal until after the incentives, which would offer American consumers up to US$12,500 each in tax credits for buying U.S.-made electric cars, are approved by Congress.
sentences.6: Opinion: If Trudeau plays tough on U.S. trade, he risks helping Trump
sentences.7: "There's a lot of complicating factors," he said in the Oval Office before his meeting with Mr. Trudeau.
sentences.8: Asked if there was room for compromise, the President said: "The answer is: I don't know, and I don't know what we're going to be dealing with, quite frankly, when it comes out of the legislation, so we'll talk about it then."

sentences.10: "We have been highlighting our concern about the proposed credit for electric vehicles uniquely made in the United States and the impact it would have on Canadian jobs and the Canadian auto industry at a time when we are investing significantly in the kinds of zero emissions vehicles that the world is going to need in the coming years," he said.
sentences.11: "Canada has highlighted real concerns about the impact it would have, not just on Canada, but the integrated industry and workers on both sides of the border."
sentences.12: The current wording of the legislation is vague on how exactly the Buy American provisions of the tax credits would work, leaving it up to the White House to make more specific regulations later on.

sentences.14: Offering the tax credits only for U.S.-made vehicles could cut Canada and Mexico out of the production of electric vehicles by encouraging auto companies to put their plants in the U.S.

sentences.22: Deputy Prime Minister Chrystia Freeland, who negotiated USMCA, has said Canada intends to aggressively lobby Democratic and Republican legislators to revamp the electric vehicle provisions in the Build Back Better legislation.

sentences.24: Mr. Trudeau and Mr. Biden met alone for 20 minutes, which Mr. Trudeau opened by pressing Mr. Biden on electric vehicles, said a Canadian government official briefed on the sit-down.

sentences.33: Despite these serious squabbles, Mr. Biden boasted about Canada-U.S. collaboration on climate change and social justice.

sentences.35: Mr. Trudeau said the two countries are "hugely aligned on climate and COVID."

The statement that tax credits will help Americans move toward a cleaner environment appeals to the emotions of the audience without addressing the specific economic or technical aspects of the policy.
The article mentions that the legislation is vague on how the Buy American provisions will work, which obscures the details and avoids clear evaluation of the policy's impact.
Mr. Biden's boasting about Canada-U.S. collaboration on climate change and social justice sidetracks from the main issue of the Buy American provisions and their impact on trade.

cases.name: Artificial intelligence makes Bill C-18, Canada's Online News Act, already outdated

sentences.1: Michael Geist holds the Canada Research Chair in Internet and E-commerce Law at the University of Ottawa, Faculty of Law.
sentences.2: The Online News Act, the government's legislative initiative to make Google and Meta pay hundreds of Canadian media companies for links to their news content, is likely to become law before politicians break for the summer later this week.
sentences.3: The lion's share of attention on Bill C-18 has thus far focused on the response of the two internet companies, as both have raised the prospect of blocking news content on their platforms if faced with new financial liability for linking.
sentences.4: Yet that focus ignores a vital new reality that may already render the bill out of date.
sentences.5: Several witnesses before the Senate committee studying the bill pointed to the emergence of generative artificial intelligence and its impact on the news business.
sentences.6: They included The Logic's David Skok and Globe and Mail publisher Phillip Crawley, who warned that links to news content on Google - a primary portal for consuming news for many - "could be disrupted in the next six to 12 months quite significantly by the difference that ChatGPT and generative AI is already making in only six months."
sentences.7: The Senate tinkered with a few minor modifications to Bill C-18, but the resulting bill is still wholly incapable of addressing the burgeoning commercial, legal and policy challenges posed by generative AI.
sentences.8: Generative AI might transform both search and news, but the not-so-secret reality of the Online News Act is that it is written for a different era entirely.
sentences.9: In fact, the bill acts as if AI does not exist at all.
sentences.10: Heritage Minister Pablo Rodriguez recently confirmed that Bill C-18 in its current form only applies to two companies: Google and Meta.
sentences.11: The current definition of "digital news intermediary" not only excludes notable internet platforms such as Twitter, Apple and TikTok, but also leading AI providers such as OpenAI (which operates ChatGPT) and Microsoft (which has incorporated AI into its Bing search engine).
sentences.12: That means there is no obligation arising out of the bill on any of those companies to negotiate agreements with Canadian news outlets.
sentences.13: Even if they were caught, the bill targets activities that are largely irrelevant for the purposes of generative AI.
sentences.14: Bill C-18 covers both reproduction of news content and "facilitating access" to news content, which includes linking, indexing or aggregating news content.
sentences.15: None of these activities describe the generative-AI process, which does not reproduce original text, need not link to original sources and does not index content in the same manner as a conventional search engine.
sentences.16: The emergence of generative AI has sparked a discussion about the prospect of licensing news content for inclusion in the large language models used by AI systems.
sentences.17: But Bill C-18 actually moves AI companies in the opposite direction, as it seems likely to wean internet intermediaries off Canadian news sources and discourages linking to original sources by upending the long-standing principle of linking to online sources as part of the free flow of information on the internet.
sentences.18: Canada can ill-afford to ignore the regulatory implications of AI.
sentences.19: As part of the AI legal landscape, there will be a need to consider the copyright and licensing implications of large language models that are essential for generative AI.
sentences.20: That issue is sure to spark a fierce debate.
sentences.21: Some will argue for the adoption of conventional licensing approaches, though any potential compensation system for news content would need to factor in the limited relative value of content from any given news source in the context of training sets with trillions of words.
sentences.22: Moreover, the implementation of significant restrictions on the development of large language models could harm Canadian aspirations to be a global AI leader and actually lead to greater bias and misinformation by relying on less-reliable training data.
sentences.23: These are critical AI policy questions, but they won't be decided by Bill C-18.
sentences.24: Rather, the government's online news bill seems increasingly likely to go down as a cautionary tale in legislative hubris.
sentences.25: It could lead to lost millions in the short term, should the internet platforms block news in response to mandated payments for links, and rendered irrelevant in the long term as it is sidelined by a generative-AI world for which it was not designed.

Explanation.explanation: The author highlights potential negative consequences of the bill while ignoring possible positive outcomes, which is an example of Cherry Picking.
The author concludes that the bill will be a legislative failure and lead to significant losses without adequate evidence to support these claims, making it a Questionable Conclusion fallacy.

cases.name: Foreign-interference office coming 'soon' but not yet ready to launch: Mendicino

sentences.1: OTTAWA â€” Public Safety Minister Marco Mendicino says the Liberals are not ready to launch the foreign-interference office they promised in last month's federal budget, amid ongoing scrutiny of allegations that Beijing interfered in recent federal elections.

Explanation.explanation: Mendicino mentions that the work has already started, which sidetracks from providing a specific timeline for the office launch.
Mendicino reiterates that Public Safety Canada is working to establish the office but does not address the urgency or provide a timeline.
Mendicino offers no timeline for the office launch, sidetracking the issue by focusing on other aspects.
Mendicino insists on getting the office up and running 'as soon as possible' but provides no evidence or timeline to support this claim.
Mendicino states they will 'remain vigilant' but does not provide concrete evidence or details on implementation.
Mendicino claims they are moving forward 'very quickly and urgently' without providing evidence or specifics.
Gaudreau appeals to urgency and the emotional need to maintain confidence in elections without addressing the specifics of the policy changes.
Mendicino highlights concerns of stigmatization within diaspora communities, evoking feelings of fear and concern without addressing the policy details.

cases.name: Sajjan says he was unaware of senator sending travel documents to Afghans because 'I wasn't reading my e-mail'

sentences.1: International Development Minister Harjit Sajjan told his fellow MPs Wednesday he did not know a Canadian senator was handing out unauthorized travel documents to hundreds of Afghans during the Taliban's rise in 2021 because he wasn't checking his email at the time.
sentences.2: Sen. Marilou McPhedran told the House immigration committee last week that Sajjan's then-chief of staff, George Young, had given her a template for a 'visa facilitation letter' that people could use to clear checkpoints on their way to the airport to escape the country.
sentences.3: She said she shared that template with several 'trusted advocates,' including the chief human rights officer with FIFA and a former Canadian Olympian.
sentences.4: McPhedran said she doesn't know how many letters were handed out, but believes it was about 640.
sentences.5: Sajjan was defence minister at the time and McPhedran said she copied him and several other ministers on many emails about her activities.
sentences.6: Sajjan told the committee he was so busy at the time he didn't have time to check his inbox.

sentences.9: MP calls explanation 'preposterous'

sentences.11: He said he was aware of authentic visa facilitation letters issued by Global Affairs Canada, but didn't authorize anyone else to use them.
sentences.12: In a statement, the Immigration Department said it issued several authentic letters directly to Afghan nationals who were eligible to come to Canada to help them clear checkpoints, but didn't allow third parties to issue them on the government's behalf.

sentences.14: Meanwhile, the government's refusal to honour the documents to allow Afghans entry to Canada is now the subject of a court case.

sentences.17: McPhedran tabled her emails with the committee but they have not yet been shared with members.
sentences.18: In a written statement sent to The Canadian Press on Wednesday, she thanked Sajjan for his commitment to getting Afghans, including women and girls at high risk, out of the country.
sentences.19: She also thanked him for his 'appreciation of his then-chief of staff George Young for working diligently to try to save lives.'
sentences.20: Sajjan said Young never told him that McPhedran was handing out visa facilitation letters but he wouldn't comment further on whether Young's alleged actions were appropriate.
sentences.21: He said he directed his staff to forward all people who were concerned about getting individuals out of Afghanistan to the appropriate interdepartmental team. He also described the frenzied atmosphere at the time.
sentences.22: NDP immigration critic Jenny Kwan said that at the end of the day, the minister is responsible for the actions of his chief of staff.
sentences.23: 'I am dismayed with the minister's comments and a little bit in shock at the level of, frankly, incompetence, if that's how he operated,' Kwan said.
sentences.24: Conservative members of the committee filed a notice of motion to call Young to testify.
sentences.25: 'This testimony is going to be critical in terms of understanding exactly what happened, if there was authorization, why he undertook this and if he actually did it to begin with,' Remple Garner said after the meeting.

Explanation.explanation: Conservative MP Michelle Remple Garner's statement 'The response 'I didn't check my email' was preposterous,' constitutes a personal attack by discrediting Sajjan's character instead of focusing on the issue at hand.
NDP immigration critic Jenny Kwan's comments criticizing Sajjan for incompetence attack his character rather than addressing the specific circumstances or validity of his explanation.

Conservative members of the committee filed a notice of motion to call Young to testify, claiming it is critical for understanding what happened. However, this conclusion may be unwarranted without more evidence linking Young's actions directly to the issue.

Michelle Remple Garner's analogy comparing Sajjan's explanation to the excuse 'the dog ate my homework' serves as a red herring by diverting attention from the substantive details of the case to a trivializing comparison.

cases.name: First two Canadian military evacuation flights leave Sudan

sentences.1: Canada has conducted its first two evacuation flights to get Canadians and other foreign nationals out of Sudan. And the federal government is promising more airlifts depending on conditions on the ground as its critics accuse it of moving too slowly.
sentences.2: At an event in Nova Scotia on Thursday, Defence Minister Anita Anand announced the first flight but offered few details. Senior officials at the Department of National Defence and Global Affairs Canada, speaking at a technical briefing later in the day in Ottawa, confirmed the second flight had left Khartoum.
sentences.3: The first evacuation flight had 45 people aboard; the second took 73 out of the war-torn country. Officials could not say how many of the evacuees on both flights were Canadian. But a confidential source told CBC News that seven Canadian citizens were on the first flight out of Sudan and 37 were on the second.
sentences.4: Both flights included people from Sudan, the U.S., Japan, the U.K. and Djibouti.
sentences.5: More flights are planned but federal officials have refused to discuss the timing.
sentences.6: Global Affairs Canada said Wednesday that up to 1,800 Canadians are stranded in Sudan and roughly 700 have asked the federal government for help to get out.
sentences.7: Officials said Thursday that after contacting virtually everyone on that list, they have narrowed down the potential number of evacuees because some have elected to stay. Approximately 108 people have said they definitely want to leave the country and another 130 are considering it.
sentences.8: Roughly 200 people on the federal government's evacuation list have made it out of the country so far, either on their own initiative or on allied military flights.
sentences.9: Indian citizens who were evacuated from Sudan arrive at the Mumbai International Airport in Mumbai, India on April 27, 2023.
sentences.10: Anand said a Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CC-130 Hercules aircraft conducted the operation. sentences.11: The evacuation flights are going to Djibouti. Global Affairs Canada is arranging to take people from there to Kenya, where they'll be responsible for their onward travel, officials said.
sentences.12: The federal government does make exceptions to that rule and offers loans to people who can't cover the cost of travel. Officials said Thursday that, so far, 30 such loans have been extended to 70 evacuees at a total cost of $170,000.
sentences.13: 'This is very good news, and I thank our Canadian Armed Forces personnel for their hard work to make this happen,' Anand said.
sentences.14: The government announced Wednesday that it will deploy up to 200 Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) troops to assist with the evacuation. That number does not include the air force and naval personnel who have been assigned to the evacuation effort, a senior defence official said Thursday.
sentences.15: Canadians and other foreign nationals have been caught in the crossfire of Sudan's civil conflict after violence broke out last week between the east African country's army and a paramilitary force.
sentences.16: The Reuters news agency reported late Thursday that Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have agreed to support a further 72-hour ceasefire. The ceasefire was due to expire at midnight. The Sudanese army agreed earlier to the extension of the shaky truce.
sentences.17: There were reports in U.K. media on Thursday that suggested Britain was prepared to keep up its evacuation effort regardless of whether a ceasefire is in place. Canadian officials were not prepared to make a similar commitment.
sentences.18: Foreign Affairs Minister Mélanie Joly said much of her time on this file over the past day has been spent talking with her counterparts about convincing both sides in the Sudanese conflict to extend the ceasefire.
sentences.19: A growing chorus of critics is asking why it took the federal government until the end of the week to kick the evacuation into gear. Joly pushed back against that criticism, saying Canadian officials have been seized with the issue at a time of multiple international crises.
sentences.20: 'There are many hot spots in the world, and there are many hot spots particularly in Africa,' she said. 'We've been at this since day one, working with other countries to find a place to do an airlift, to secure that place, to make sure that we would be working together ...
sentences.21: 'At the end of the day, I'm not into Monday morning quarterbacking. My job is to get Canadians outside of Sudan and we will make sure that that's the case.'
sentences.22: A senior defence official, speaking on background at a technical briefing Thursday, said military and Global Affairs officials began meeting on Sudan 12 days ago. The military transport aircraft, a contingent of special forces soldiers and other troops have been on the ground in Djibouti supporting diplomats for a week.

Explanation.explanation: Joly's statement about 'multiple international crises' diverts attention from the specific issue of why the evacuation took time to start.
Anand's expression of gratitude to the Canadian Armed Forces personnel appeals to emotions rather than addressing the criticisms of the evacuation's timing.

cases.name: Toronto-area housing developments at risk as lenders accuse StateView Homes of wrongdoing

sentences.1: The future of hundreds of unbuilt townhouses is in limbo as Toronto-area home builder StateView Homes deals with fallout caused by an alleged 'cheque-kiting' scheme that ran up debts of $37-million.
sentences.2: A lawsuit filed by Toronto-Dominion Bank TD-T on March 24 alleges a series of 'fraudulent cheques' were used to manipulate the bank's overdraft system, costing the bank $37-million between April, 2022, and March, 2023.
sentences.3: TD claims a series of bad cheques from several StateView business accounts at Royal Bank of Canada RY-T were deposited in dozens of TD accounts associated with StateView real estate projects.
sentences.4: The lawsuit claims StateView - founded in 2010 by brothers Dino and Carlo Taurasi with friend and chief financial officer Daniel Ciccone - repeatedly deposited cheques written on the RBC accounts into the TD accounts, and the Canadian Clearing and Settlement Systems (which handles transactions between financial institutions) conditionally credited the value of the cheques to the TD account 'pending final settlement.'
sentences.5: TD alleges that before the transfer cleared, however, StateView moved the conditionally credited money out - either to a different account at another bank, or wire transferred it to a third party - and then stopped payment on the original RBC cheques.
sentences.6: To avoid detection of this scheme, called cheque-kiting, TD further alleges StateView processed a large volume of 'sham transactions' between other TD accounts.
sentences.7: None of the allegations have been tested in court, and TD and its lawyers at McCarthy Tétrault LLP declined to comment as the matter is still before the courts.
sentences.8: StateView didn't comment on allegations of cheque fraud outlined by TD but in an e-mailed statement vice-president of marketing Darryl Orian said: 'Unfortunately, as the situation is ongoing, StateView Homes cannot comment on the circumstances or details leading to a settlement with TD.'
sentences.9: StateView issued a fuller statement Tuesday addressing 'rumours and speculation around the solvency of the organization,' stressing it was not declaring bankruptcy.
sentences.10: StateView also said Mr. Ciccone, the CFO, has been relieved of his position in the company.
sentences.11: 'StateView has faced significant disruptions in its treasury functions at its current financial institution, which has unfortunately resulted in StateView's liquidity being constrained,' the statement reads.
sentences.12: 'StateView intends to complete all projects currently under construction and is actively working with our partners to move forward with as many projects as possible while also recognizing the position of our lenders.'
sentences.13: In the wake of TD's filings, StateView is facing demands for repayment from at least two other lenders that could see an unfinished townhouse project (Nao Towns Phase II in Markham, Ont., with 96 units) pushed into insolvency.
sentences.14: Lawyers for Dorr Capital Corp. and Atrium Mortgage Investment Corp. have requested a hearing - scheduled for Friday at Ontario's Superior Court of Justice - to argue for the appointment of a receiver to ensure the lenders can collect $24.4-million that the companies say they are owed.
sentences.15: According to a statement of claim filed by Dorr and Atrium, StateView missed a $277,598.63 loan payment for the Nao project on April 1, after which it registered a new mortgage (from TD) against the property without written consent or notice.
sentences.16: Moreover, Dorr and Atrium describe the alleged cheque-kiting scheme as 'a material adverse change … relating to the debtor and the guarantors' because the $37-million StateView owes TD is 'a debt and liability arising out of fraud.'
sentences.17: StateView's website says it has completed construction on nine projects since its founding, and the Home Construction Regulatory Authority's registry shows it has 279 completed units, including 28 handed over in 2023.
sentences.18: StateView also has several Ontario projects under construction, sold out or 'fully reserved' that may now be subject to reorganization of StateView's debts.

Explanation.explanation: The text selectively presents data on ventilator deaths without considering broader context or contradictory evidence, like improvements in treatment protocols over time.

The text implies that not using ventilators would easily allow for alternative treatments like ivermectin or hydroxychloroquine, without considering the complexities and risks involved.
